diff --git a/bin/automouse/README.md b/bin/automouse/README.md
index ea27f2f7b6..e5f916a017 100644
--- a/bin/automouse/README.md
+++ b/bin/automouse/README.md
@@ -15,6 +15,8 @@ queue/ ──► run ──► (per plan) claude -p impl  ──► handoff/<pla
 queue ◄──── queue-reorder-ui (browser drag-reorder UI, writes queue order)
 ```
 
+When `bin/plan-now` queues a JSB parity port plan (slug `jsb-port-pl-<n>`), it starts `bin/automouse/run plan <slug>` right away under its own launchd label. It skips that start while automouse is disarmed or another runner is live, and the plan then waits for the nightly run.
+
 ## Scripts
 
 | Script | Role |
diff --git a/bin/plan-now b/bin/plan-now
index d6b8120aaf..91c6ba2fdc 100755
--- a/bin/plan-now
+++ b/bin/plan-now
@@ -7,6 +7,8 @@
 # Usage:
 #   bin/plan-now <prompt-file>              # run it, then queue for automouse if the
 #                                           #   run exits clean AND check-plan passes

 #   bin/plan-now --implement <prompt-file>  # ... but leave the plan on disk, unqueued
 #   bin/plan-now --queue <prompt-file>      # explicit form of the default
 #   bin/plan-now --model opus <prompt-file> # orchestrator model (default claude-sonnet-5-5)
@@ -543,6 +545,16 @@ REVIEW_ROUTE_DEFAULT=$(grep -oE "'/discordPlanReviewDM'" \
     # queue seam is what lets bin/test-plan-now reach the queued-vs-not fork at all.
     # AUTOMOUSE_LOGIN_PROBE_CMD and LOGIN_PROBE_* stub the login probe the same way.
     printf 'AUTOMOUSE_QUEUE=%q\n' "${PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_QUEUE:-$ROOT/bin/automouse/queue}"
+    # Test seams for the parity-port kick. Unset and empty both mean the real
+    # launch through ljob_submit. They are baked so a stub survives launchd's
+    # empty env.
+    printf 'AUTOMOUSE_KICK=%q\n' "${PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_KICK:-}"
+    printf 'KICK_RUN_BIN=%q\n' "$ROOT/bin/automouse/run"
+    printf 'KICK_DRY_RUN=%q\n' "${PLAN_NOW_DRY_RUN:-0}"
+    printf 'KICK_STATE_DIR=%q\n' "${AUTOMOUSE_STATE_DIR:-$HOME/.claude/projects/-Users-ajaynicolas-GitHub-IBL5/automouse}"
+    printf 'KICK_LAUNCHCTL=%q\n' "${PLAN_NOW_KICK_LAUNCHCTL:-launchctl}"
+    printf 'KICK_PGREP=%q\n' "${PLAN_NOW_KICK_PGREP:-pgrep}"
+    printf 'KICK_LAUNCHD_LIB=%q\n' "$PLAN_NOW_LIB_DIR/launchd-job.sh"
     printf 'DISCORD_DM=%q\n' "$(dm_bin "$ROOT/bin" PLAN_NOW_DISCORD_DM)"
     printf 'CLAUDE_BIN=%q\n' "${PLAN_NOW_CLAUDE:-claude}"
     printf 'PLAN_SLUG_RE=%q\n' "$PLAN_SLUG_RE"
@@ -560,6 +572,66 @@ REVIEW_ROUTE_DEFAULT=$(grep -oE "'/discordPlanReviewDM'" \
     printf 'REVIEW_ROUTE=%q\n' "${PLAN_NOW_REVIEW_ROUTE:-$REVIEW_ROUTE_DEFAULT}"
     declare -f ljob_dm_ready ljob_dm_send
     cat <<'RUNNER_EOF'
+# --- automouse kick for JSB parity port plans --------------------------------
+# A queued jsb-port-pl-<digits>[-<n>] plan starts `bin/automouse/run plan <slug>`
+# right away, detached under its own launchd label, instead of waiting for the
+# nightly run. Every skip leaves the plan queued, so the nightly run still takes it.
+# Returns 0 on launch or skip; nonzero only when the launch itself failed.
+KICK_PORT_RE='^jsb-port-pl-[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?$'
+KICK_RUNNER_RE='bin/automouse/run( |$)'
+KICK_LAUNCHED=""
+plan_now_kick_port() {
+    local kplan="$1" kslug know kout kpid krearm klabel klog kscript krc
+    kslug=$(basename "${kplan%.md}")
+    # Guard 1: a dry-run runner with no stub never launches a real run.
+    if [ "$KICK_DRY_RUN" = "1" ] && [ -z "$AUTOMOUSE_KICK" ]; then return 0; fi
+    # Guard 2: only parity port plans kick. Silent, so non-port logs are unchanged.
+    [[ "$kslug" =~ $KICK_PORT_RE ]] || return 0
+    # Guard 3: never override a disarm. An unreadable epoch fails safe (skip).
+    if [ -f "$KICK_STATE_DIR/.disarmed-until" ]; then
+        krearm=$(awk '/^rearm_epoch=/ && !f {sub(/^rearm_epoch=/, ""); print; f=1}' "$KICK_STATE_DIR/.disarmed-until")
+        case "$krearm" in
+            ''|*[!0-9]*)
+                echo "plan-now: automouse kick skipped: unreadable disarm breadcrumb; the plan stays queued."
+                return 0 ;;
+        esac
+        know=$(date +%s)
+        if [ "$krearm" -gt "$know" ]; then
+            echo "plan-now: automouse kick skipped: automouse is disarmed until epoch $krearm; the plan stays queued."
+            return 0
+        fi
+    fi
+    # Guard 4a: the nightly job is mid-run (same probe as automouse_running_pid).
+    kout=$("$KICK_LAUNCHCTL" list com.ibl5.automouse 2>/dev/null || true)
+    kpid=$(printf '%s\n' "$kout" | sed -n 's/.*"PID"[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*\([0-9][0-9]*\);.*/\1/p' | head -1)
+    if [ -n "$kpid" ]; then
+        echo "plan-now: automouse kick skipped: the nightly automouse run is live (PID $kpid); the plan stays queued."
+        return 0
+    fi
+    # Guard 4b: any other runner (manual run plan, a run schedule one-shot, an
+    # earlier kick). pgrep exit 1 = provably none; any other exit = undecidable = skip,
+    # the same convention as ljob_pgrep_alive in bin/lib/launchd-job.sh.
+    if "$KICK_PGREP" -f "$KICK_RUNNER_RE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then krc=0; else krc=$?; fi
+    if [ "$krc" -ne 1 ]; then
+        echo "plan-now: automouse kick skipped: another automouse runner is live (pgrep exit $krc); the plan stays queued."
+        return 0
+    fi
+    if [ -n "$AUTOMOUSE_KICK" ]; then
+        "$AUTOMOUSE_KICK" "$kslug" || return 1
+    else
+        . "$KICK_LAUNCHD_LIB" || return 1
+        klabel="com.ibl5.automouse-kick-$(ljob_safe_slug "$kslug")"
+        mkdir -p "$KICK_STATE_DIR/logs" || return 1
+        klog="$KICK_STATE_DIR/logs/kick-$kslug.log"
+        kscript=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/plan-now-kick.XXXXXX") || return 1
+        printf '#!/bin/bash\nrm -f -- "$0"\nexec %q plan %q\n' "$KICK_RUN_BIN" "$kslug" > "$kscript" || return 1
+        chmod +x "$kscript" || return 1
+        ljob_submit "$klabel" "$klog" "$kscript" || return 1
+    fi
+    KICK_LAUNCHED="$kslug"
+    echo "plan-now: automouse kick started: run plan $kslug, detached; the plan stays queued until that run claims it."
+}
+# --- end automouse kick -------------------------------------------------------
 # launchd runs with a minimal env — same PATH prelude bin/automouse/run uses.
 export PATH="/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:/Applications/cmux.app/Contents/Resources/bin:$PATH"
 cd "$ROOT" || exit 1
@@ -893,6 +965,11 @@ elif [ -n "$plan" ]; then
                 echo "plan-now: queued for automouse — it will implement this plan and open its PR."
                 echo "plan-now: to pull it back out: bin/automouse/queue remove $(basename "${plan%.md}")"
                 DM_NEXT="queued for automouse"
+                if ! plan_now_kick_port "$plan"; then
+                    echo "plan-now: WARNING — kick failed; the plan stays queued for the nightly automouse run."
+                elif [ -n "$KICK_LAUNCHED" ]; then
+                    DM_NEXT="queued for automouse; kicked run plan $KICK_LAUNCHED"
+                fi
             else
                 echo "plan-now: WARNING — check-plan passed but automouse-queue failed; the plan is on disk, unqueued."
                 DM_ICON="⚠️"; DM_VERDICT="ok — check-plan PASSED, but automouse-queue FAILED"
@@ -1046,6 +1123,11 @@ else
                     echo "plan-now: queued for automouse (recovered plan) — it will implement this plan and open its PR."
                     echo "plan-now: to pull it back out: bin/automouse/queue remove $(basename "${recovered%.md}")"
                     DM_NEXT="queued for automouse"
+                    if ! plan_now_kick_port "$recovered"; then
+                        echo "plan-now: WARNING — kick failed; the plan stays queued for the nightly automouse run."
+                    elif [ -n "$KICK_LAUNCHED" ]; then
+                        DM_NEXT="queued for automouse; kicked run plan $KICK_LAUNCHED"
+                    fi
                 else
                     echo "plan-now: WARNING — check-plan passed but automouse-queue failed; the recovered plan is on disk, unqueued."
                     DM_VERDICT="degraded (recovered) — check-plan PASSED, but automouse-queue FAILED"
diff --git a/bin/test-plan-now b/bin/test-plan-now
index 14b0e65ac4..cbb19ee222 100755
--- a/bin/test-plan-now
+++ b/bin/test-plan-now
@@ -2308,6 +2308,247 @@ else
     fail "L-7 probe precedes the spawn (probe=$l7_probe spawn=$l7_spawn)"
 fi
 
+# === automouse kick cases (plan-now-kick-automouse-parity-ports) ===
+# A queued jsb-port-pl-<n> plan starts `bin/automouse/run plan <slug>` right away.
+# Every launch goes through a stub (PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_KICK), so no case starts a
+# real automouse run. A PATH-first launchctl recorder catches a guard that regresses
+# into the real launchd path.
+echo "── automouse kick: a queued parity port plan starts its own run ──"
+
+KT=$(mktemp -d "$TMP/kick.XXXXXX")
+mkdir -p "$KT/bin" "$KT/state"
+cat > "$KT/bin/launchctl" <<KT_LCTL_EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "$KT/launchctl.calls"
+exit 1
+KT_LCTL_EOF
+KICK_STUB="$KT/kick-ok"
+cat > "$KICK_STUB" <<KT_OK_EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+printf '%s\n' "\$1" >> "$KT/kick.args"
+exit 0
+KT_OK_EOF
+KICK_FAIL_STUB="$KT/kick-fail"
+printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 7\n' > "$KICK_FAIL_STUB"
+LAUNCHCTL_IDLE="$KT/lc-idle"
+printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 113\n' > "$LAUNCHCTL_IDLE"
+LAUNCHCTL_BUSY="$KT/lc-busy"
+cat > "$LAUNCHCTL_BUSY" <<'KT_BUSY_EOF'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+printf '{\n\t"PID" = 4242;\n\t"Label" = "com.ibl5.automouse";\n};\n'
+exit 0
+KT_BUSY_EOF
+PGREP_STUB="$KT/pgrep"
+cat > "$PGREP_STUB" <<KT_PGREP_EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+[ "\$1" = "-f" ] || exit 3
+grep -qE -- "\$2" "$KT/procs"
+KT_PGREP_EOF
+chmod +x "$KT/bin/launchctl" "$KICK_STUB" "$KICK_FAIL_STUB" "$LAUNCHCTL_IDLE" "$LAUNCHCTL_BUSY" "$PGREP_STUB"
+printf '# stub plan\n' > "$KT/one-liner.plan.md"
+KICK_STALE_PLAN="$KT/stale-port.plan.md"
+cp "$GOOD_PLAN" "$KICK_STALE_PLAN"
+printf '\nThe sweep also touches `ibl5/no-such-file-for-kick-test.php` in passing.\n' >> "$KICK_STALE_PLAN"
+KICK_PROMPT="$KT/port-prompt.md"
+{
+    printf '/plan Port JSB routine for the kick test\n'
+    printf -- '- Branch slug: `jsb-port-pl-0042`. Base: `master`.\n'
+} > "$KICK_PROMPT"
+
+# Defaults for every kick case. A case overrides one through the extra VAR=value
+# arguments of kick_run, which reach the dry-run call where the seams are baked.
+export PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_KICK="$KICK_STUB" PLAN_NOW_KICK_LAUNCHCTL="$LAUNCHCTL_IDLE"
+export PLAN_NOW_KICK_PGREP="$PGREP_STUB" AUTOMOUSE_STATE_DIR="$KT/state"
+KICK_SAVE_PATH="$PATH"
+KICK_SAVE_TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-}"
+export PATH="$KT/bin:$PATH" TMPDIR="$KT"
+
+kick_reset() {
+    rm -f "$KT/kick.args" "$KT/launchctl.calls"
+    : > "$KT/procs"
+    rm -rf "$KT/state"; mkdir -p "$KT/state"
+}
+kick_ran() { [ -f "$KT/kick.args" ]; }
+kick_args() { cat "$KT/kick.args" 2>/dev/null; }
+
+# kick_run <slug> [VAR=value | -u VAR ...] -> KOUT (runner output), KRC (runner exit
+# status), KRUNNER_TEXT (the generated runner). $KSRC picks the plan the stub model
+# writes (default: one that passes check-plan); $KQFAIL=1 makes the queue stub fail.
+kick_run() {
+    local slug="$1"; shift
+    local plan="$PLANS/$slug.md" dry runner
+    rm -f "$PLANS"/*.md
+    : > "$DM_LOG"
+    dry=$(env "$@" PLAN_NOW_DRY_RUN=1 PLAN_NOW_CLAUDE="$STUB" PLAN_NOW_PLANS_DIR="$PLANS" \
+              PLAN_NOW_DISCORD_DM="$DM_STUB" PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_QUEUE="$QUEUE_STUB" \
+              "$PLAN_NOW" --queue "$PROMPT" 2>&1)
+    runner=$(printf '%s\n' "$dry" | sed -n 's/^  runner: //p')
+    [ -x "$runner" ] || { KOUT="no runner: $dry"; KRC=99; return 1; }
+    rm -f "$KT/launchctl.calls"
+    KRUNNER_TEXT=$(cat "$runner")
+    KRC=0
+    KOUT=$(STUB_PLAN="$plan" STUB_TAIL="PLAN_FILE: $plan" STUB_PLAN_SRC="${KSRC:-$GOOD_PLAN}" \
+        QUEUE_FAIL="${KQFAIL:-}" bash "$runner" 2>&1) || KRC=$?
+    rm -f "$runner"
+}
+# kick_run_recovered <plan-basename> [VAR=value ...]: the leg-B recovery path, where the
+# run omitted PLAN_FILE: and the runner adopts the plan the run left in $PLANS.
+kick_run_recovered() {
+    local name="$1"; shift
+    local dry runner
+    plans_reset
+    : > "$DM_LOG"
+    dry=$(env "$@" PLAN_NOW_DRY_RUN=1 PLAN_NOW_CLAUDE="$STUB" PLAN_NOW_PLANS_DIR="$PLANS" \
+              PLAN_NOW_DISCORD_DM="$DM_STUB" PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_QUEUE="$QUEUE_STUB" \
+              "$PLAN_NOW" --queue "$KICK_PROMPT" 2>&1)
+    runner=$(printf '%s\n' "$dry" | sed -n 's/^  runner: //p')
+    [ -x "$runner" ] || { KOUT="no runner: $dry"; KRC=99; return 1; }
+    rm -f "$KT/launchctl.calls"
+    KRC=0
+    KOUT=$(STUB_NO_PLAN=1 STUB_TAIL="" STUB_PLANFILE="$PLANS/$name" STUB_PLANFILE_SRC="$GOOD_PLAN" \
+        bash "$runner" 2>&1) || KRC=$?
+    rm -f "$runner"
+}
+
+KICK_STARTED_0042="plan-now: automouse kick started: run plan jsb-port-pl-0042, detached; the plan stays queued until that run claims it."
+
+# K1 a port plan that queues kicks once.
+kick_reset
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+want    "K1 port plan: log names the kick"           "$KOUT" "$KICK_STARTED_0042"
+want    "K1 port plan: the queue stub saw the plan"  "$KOUT" "automouse-queue (stub): queued $PLANS/jsb-port-pl-0042.md"
+want    "K1 port plan: DM names the kicked run"      "$(dm)" "queued for automouse; kicked run plan jsb-port-pl-0042"
+[ "$(kick_args)" = "jsb-port-pl-0042" ] && ok "K1 port plan: exactly one kick for the slug" \
+    || fail "K1 port plan: exactly one kick for the slug (got: $(kick_args))"
+K1_RC="$KRC"
+kick_reset
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-7
+[ "$(kick_args)" = "jsb-port-pl-7" ] && ok "K1 single-digit port slug kicks once" \
+    || fail "K1 single-digit port slug kicks once (got: $(kick_args))"
+
+# K2 a non-port plan queues and never kicks.
+kick_reset
+kick_run demo-slug
+want    "K2 non-port plan still queues"      "$KOUT" "automouse-queue (stub): queued $PLANS/demo-slug.md"
+want_no "K2 non-port plan: no kick in the log" "$KOUT" "automouse kick"
+want    "K2 non-port plan: DM says queued"   "$(dm)" "queued for automouse"
+want_no "K2 non-port plan: DM names no kick" "$(dm)" "kicked"
+kick_ran && fail "K2 non-port plan: the kick stub ran" || ok "K2 non-port plan: the kick stub never ran"
+
+# K3 a port plan that never reaches the queue is never kicked.
+kick_reset
+KSRC="$KT/one-liner.plan.md" kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+want    "K3 check-plan FAILED: not queued"   "$KOUT" "NOT queued"
+kick_ran && fail "K3 check-plan FAILED: kicked" || ok "K3 check-plan FAILED: never kicked"
+kick_reset
+KSRC="$KICK_STALE_PLAN" kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+want    "K3 staleness FAILED: named in the log" "$KOUT" "check-plan-staleness FAILED"
+kick_ran && fail "K3 staleness FAILED: kicked" || ok "K3 staleness FAILED: never kicked"
+kick_reset
+KQFAIL=1 kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+want    "K3 queue call FAILED: named in the log" "$KOUT" "automouse-queue failed"
+kick_ran && fail "K3 queue call FAILED: kicked" || ok "K3 queue call FAILED: never kicked"
+
+# K4a the nightly job is mid-run: skip, the plan stays queued.
+kick_reset
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042 PLAN_NOW_KICK_LAUNCHCTL="$LAUNCHCTL_BUSY"
+want    "K4a nightly live: skip line"        "$KOUT" "plan-now: automouse kick skipped: the nightly automouse run is live (PID 4242); the plan stays queued."
+want    "K4a nightly live: plan still queued" "$KOUT" "automouse-queue (stub): queued $PLANS/jsb-port-pl-0042.md"
+kick_ran && fail "K4a nightly live: kicked" || ok "K4a nightly live: no kick"
+
+# K4b any other runner is live: skip. pgrep exit 1 means none; any other exit skips.
+kick_reset
+printf '/bin/bash /Users/x/GitHub/IBL5/bin/automouse/run plan jsb-port-pl-0007\n' > "$KT/procs"
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+want    "K4b runner live: skip line"         "$KOUT" "plan-now: automouse kick skipped: another automouse runner is live (pgrep exit 0); the plan stays queued."
+kick_ran && fail "K4b runner live: kicked" || ok "K4b runner live: no kick"
+kick_reset
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042 PLAN_NOW_KICK_PGREP="$KT/no-such-pgrep"
+want    "K4b pgrep missing: skip line"       "$KOUT" "another automouse runner is live (pgrep exit 127); the plan stays queued."
+kick_ran && fail "K4b pgrep missing: kicked" || ok "K4b pgrep missing: no kick"
+kick_reset
+printf 'bash bin/automouse/runner-old\nbash bin/test-automouse-single\n' > "$KT/procs"
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+[ "$(kick_args)" = "jsb-port-pl-0042" ] && ok "K4b near-miss process lines still kick once" \
+    || fail "K4b near-miss process lines still kick once (got: $(kick_args))"
+
+# K5 a failed kick is logged, and nothing else about the run changes.
+kick_reset
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042 PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_KICK="$KICK_FAIL_STUB"
+want    "K5 kick failed: warning line"       "$KOUT" "plan-now: WARNING — kick failed; the plan stays queued for the nightly automouse run."
+want    "K5 kick failed: plan still queued"  "$KOUT" "automouse-queue (stub): queued $PLANS/jsb-port-pl-0042.md"
+want    "K5 kick failed: DM says queued"     "$(dm)" "queued for automouse"
+want_no "K5 kick failed: DM names no kick"   "$(dm)" "kicked"
+[ "$KRC" = "$K1_RC" ] && ok "K5 kick failed: runner exit status unchanged ($KRC)" \
+    || fail "K5 kick failed: runner exit status unchanged (got $KRC, K1 had $K1_RC)"
+
+# K6 never override a disarm.
+kick_reset
+KT_FUTURE=$(( $(date +%s) + 3600 ))
+printf 'rearm_epoch=%s\n' "$KT_FUTURE" > "$KT/state/.disarmed-until"
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+want    "K6 disarmed: skip line"             "$KOUT" "plan-now: automouse kick skipped: automouse is disarmed until epoch $KT_FUTURE; the plan stays queued."
+kick_ran && fail "K6 disarmed: kicked" || ok "K6 disarmed: no kick"
+kick_reset
+printf 'rearm_epoch=1\n' > "$KT/state/.disarmed-until"
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+[ "$(kick_args)" = "jsb-port-pl-0042" ] && ok "K6 a past rearm_epoch does not block" \
+    || fail "K6 a past rearm_epoch does not block (got: $(kick_args))"
+kick_reset
+printf 'rearm_epoch=soon\n' > "$KT/state/.disarmed-until"
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042
+want    "K6 garbage epoch: skip line"        "$KOUT" "plan-now: automouse kick skipped: unreadable disarm breadcrumb; the plan stays queued."
+kick_ran && fail "K6 garbage epoch: kicked" || ok "K6 garbage epoch: no kick"
+
+# K7 a recovered port plan kicks too.
+kick_reset
+kick_run_recovered jsb-port-pl-0042-2.md
+want    "K7 recovered plan: queued"          "$KOUT" "queued for automouse (recovered plan)"
+want    "K7 recovered plan: log names the kick" "$KOUT" "plan-now: automouse kick started: run plan jsb-port-pl-0042-2, detached"
+[ "$(kick_args)" = "jsb-port-pl-0042-2" ] && ok "K7 recovered plan: exactly one kick for the slug" \
+    || fail "K7 recovered plan: exactly one kick for the slug (got: $(kick_args))"
+
+# K8 near-miss slugs reach the queue and never kick.
+for k8_slug in jsb-port-pl-12a x-jsb-port-pl-12 jsb-port-pl-12-final; do
+    kick_reset
+    kick_run "$k8_slug"
+    want "K8 $k8_slug: reached the queue" "$KOUT" "automouse-queue (stub): queued $PLANS/$k8_slug.md"
+    kick_ran && fail "K8 $k8_slug: kicked" || ok "K8 $k8_slug: no kick"
+done
+# The regex keeps its optional -<n> tail and its end anchor.
+want_no "K8 the port regex is not the tail-less form" "$KRUNNER_TEXT" "'^jsb-port-pl-[0-9]+'"
+
+# K9 the env seam: unset and empty both bake an empty value, and a dry-run runner
+# with no stub never reaches launchd.
+kick_reset
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042 -u PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_KICK -u PLAN_NOW_KICK_LAUNCHCTL -u PLAN_NOW_KICK_PGREP
+want    "K9 seam unset bakes an empty value" "$KRUNNER_TEXT" "AUTOMOUSE_KICK=''"
+[ ! -e "$KT/launchctl.calls" ] && ok "K9 seam unset: launchctl untouched" || fail "K9 seam unset: launchctl untouched"
+want_no "K9 seam unset: no kick in the log"  "$KOUT" "automouse kick"
+kick_reset
+kick_run jsb-port-pl-0042 PLAN_NOW_AUTOMOUSE_KICK= -u PLAN_NOW_KICK_LAUNCHCTL -u PLAN_NOW_KICK_PGREP
+want    "K9 seam empty bakes an empty value" "$KRUNNER_TEXT" "AUTOMOUSE_KICK=''"
+[ ! -e "$KT/launchctl.calls" ] && ok "K9 seam empty: launchctl untouched" || fail "K9 seam empty: launchctl untouched"
+want_no "K9 seam empty: no kick in the log"  "$KOUT" "automouse kick"
+if ls "$KT"/plan-now-kick.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    fail "K9 dry-run guard: a plan-now-kick script was written"
+else
+    ok "K9 dry-run guard: no plan-now-kick script written"
+fi

+#!/bin/bash
+#
+# bin/check-replay-spec-registry-additions: keep new gates out of the REPLAY_SPECS registry.
+#
+# Fails when the working tree's REPLAY_SPECS in tools/postplan-harness/harness/gate_backtest.py
+# holds a key the merge-base copy lacks. gate_backtest.py is an arming path, so a registry edit
+# holds the PR as SELF-GOVERNING. A new gate declares its replay in its own script instead,
+# with a comment header:
+#   # gate-backtest-argv: <argv>
+#   # gate-backtest: not-replayable <reason>
+# Existing keys never block: value edits, reformatting and removals pass. A key line ending in
+# "# replay-spec-ok: <reason>" with a non-empty reason is exempt, for a spec field a header
+# cannot carry. A string-valued key (a not-replayable string in place of a spec) fails too.
+#
+# The key scan is a line match on quoted bin/ keys inside the REPLAY_SPECS block. It exits 2
+# when the block is missing, so a renamed dict fails loudly and never passes silently.
+#
+# Extend-before-add (meta-tooling-bar.md): distinct trigger (one registry dict in one Python file); no sibling check reads gate_backtest.py.
+#
+# gate-backtest-argv: --since={base}
+#
+# Bash 3.2 safe (macOS /bin/bash): no mapfile, no associative arrays, no ${x,,}.
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 = pass, 1 = new key found, 2 = usage or git error.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+usage() {
+    echo "usage: bin/check-replay-spec-registry-additions --since=<ref>"
+}
+
+die() {
+    echo "check-replay-spec-registry-additions: $1" >&2
+    exit 2
+}
+
+since=""
+if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
+    usage >&2
+    die "use --since=<ref>"
+fi
+for arg in "$@"; do
+    case "$arg" in
+        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+        --since=?*) since="${arg#--since=}" ;;
+        --since=) die "use --since=<ref>" ;;
+        --since) die "use --since=<ref> (the = form is required)" ;;
+        -*) die "unknown option: $arg" ;;
+        *) die "use --since=<ref> (unexpected argument: $arg)" ;;
+    esac
+done
+[ -n "$since" ] || die "use --since=<ref>"
+
+root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "not inside a git repository"
+cd "$root"
+
+git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${since}^{commit}" >/dev/null || die "cannot resolve ref: $since"
+mb=$(git merge-base "$since" HEAD 2>/dev/null) || die "no merge-base (shallow clone?)"
+
+tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
+
+P=tools/postplan-harness/harness/gate_backtest.py
+
+# List the REPLAY_SPECS keys found on stdin, one per line, sorted.
+# A key line opens (after indentation) with a quoted bin/ path and a colon.
+# Comment lines never match. Lines outside the REPLAY_SPECS block never match.
+# A key line ending in "# replay-spec-ok: <non-empty reason>" is skipped.
+extract_keys() {
+    awk '
+        /^REPLAY_SPECS([: ].*)?=[[:space:]]*\{[[:space:]]*$/ { inblk = 1; found = 1; next }
+        inblk && /^\}/ { inblk = 0; next }
+        inblk && /^[[:space:]]*["'\'']bin\/[^"'\'']+["'\''][[:space:]]*:/ {
+            if ($0 ~ /#[[:space:]]*replay-spec-ok:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]]/) next
+            s = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*["'\'']/, "", s); sub(/["'\''].*$/, "", s); print s
+        }
+        END { if (!found) exit 3 }
+    ' | LC_ALL=C sort -u
+}
+
+if [ ! -f "$P" ]; then
+    echo "check-replay-spec-registry-additions: $P absent; nothing to check"
+    exit 0
+fi
+
+if ! extract_keys < "$P" > "$tmp/head.keys"; then
+    die "no REPLAY_SPECS block in $P (renamed?)"
+fi
+
+if git cat-file -e "$mb:$P" 2>/dev/null; then
+    git show "$mb:$P" > "$tmp/base.src" || die "cannot read $P at $mb"
+    if ! extract_keys < "$tmp/base.src" > "$tmp/base.keys"; then
+        die "no REPLAY_SPECS block in $P at the merge-base"
+    fi
+else
+    : > "$tmp/base.keys"
+fi
+
+added=$(comm -13 "$tmp/base.keys" "$tmp/head.keys")
+
+if [ -z "$added" ]; then
+    echo "check-replay-spec-registry-additions: no new REPLAY_SPECS keys"
+    exit 0
+fi
+
+{
+    echo "check-replay-spec-registry-additions: this change adds REPLAY_SPECS key(s) to $P:"
+    echo "$added" | sed 's/^/  /'
+    cat <<'DENY_EOF'
+Declare the replay in the gate script itself, as a comment header:
+  # gate-backtest-argv: <argv, e.g. --since={base}>
+or, for a gate the replay cannot run:
+  # gate-backtest: not-replayable <reason>
+Then drop the registry line. gate_backtest.py is an arming path, so editing it holds the PR as SELF-GOVERNING.
+If the entry needs a field a header cannot carry, end its line with: # replay-spec-ok: <reason>
+DENY_EOF
+} >&2
+exit 1

+#!/bin/bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# Test harness for bin/check-replay-spec-registry-additions (the REPLAY_SPECS additions gate).
+# Follows bin/test-check-pipefail-assignment-guard style.
+#
+# Each case builds a throwaway repo under a mktemp dir. The repo holds a fixture
+# tools/postplan-harness/harness/gate_backtest.py committed as the base. The case edits the
+# working tree, runs the gate by absolute path with --since=<base sha>, and asserts the exit
+# code plus an output substring. Nothing is written inside the IBL5 tree.
+
+PASS=0
+FAIL=0
+CHK="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/check-replay-spec-registry-additions"
+GB=tools/postplan-harness/harness/gate_backtest.py
+
+pass() { echo "PASS $1"; PASS=$((PASS + 1)); }
+fail() { echo "FAIL $1"; FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); }
+
+T=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+N=0
+R=""
+BASE=""
+
+# Build a fresh fixture repo in $R and record the base commit in $BASE.
+fresh() {
+    N=$((N + 1))
+    R="$T/repo$N"
+    mkdir -p "$R/$(dirname "$GB")" "$R/bin"
+    cat > "$R/$GB" <<'FIXTURE_EOF'
+"""fixture"""
+REPLAY_SPECS: dict[str, object] = {
+    "bin/check-a": _SINCE,
+    "bin/check-b": _TREE,
+    "bin/check-c": ReplaySpec(
+        argv=("x",),
+    ),
+}
+
+_OTHER = {
+    "bin/check-z": 1,
+}
+FIXTURE_EOF
+    git -C "$R" init -q
+    git -C "$R" config gc.auto 0
+    git -C "$R" config maintenance.auto false
+    git -C "$R" config commit.gpgsign false
+    git -C "$R" add -A
+    git -C "$R" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm base
+    BASE=$(git -C "$R" rev-parse HEAD)
+}
+
+# Insert a line after the first line containing the literal text $1 (fixed string).
+add_after() {
+    awk -v pat="$1" -v add="$2" '{ print } index($0, pat) && !done { print add; done = 1 }' \
+        "$R/$GB" > "$R/$GB.new"
+    mv "$R/$GB.new" "$R/$GB"
+}
+
+# Run a check script ($1) with the remaining args inside $R. Sets RC and OUT.
+run_with() {
+    local script="$1"
+    shift
+    RC=0
+    OUT=$(cd "$R" && "$script" "$@" 2>&1) || RC=$?
+}
+
+# Assert the exit code ($2) and, when given, an output substring ($3).
+expect() {
+    local name="$1" want_rc="$2" want_sub="${3:-}"
+    if [ "$RC" != "$want_rc" ]; then
+        fail "$name (exit $RC, wanted $want_rc: $OUT)"
+        return
+    fi
+    if [ -n "$want_sub" ] && ! grep -qF -- "$want_sub" <<< "$OUT"; then
+        fail "$name (output lacks '$want_sub': $OUT)"
+        return
+    fi
+    pass "$name"
+}
+
+# ---- cases that must fail (exit 1) ----
+
+fresh
+add_after '"bin/check-a": _SINCE,' '    "bin/check-new": _SINCE,'
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+if [ "$RC" = 1 ] && grep -qF -- 'bin/check-new' <<< "$OUT" && grep -qF -- '# gate-backtest-argv:' <<< "$OUT"; then
+    pass added_key_fails
+else
+    fail "added_key_fails (exit $RC: $OUT)"
+fi
+
+fresh
+add_after '"bin/check-a": _SINCE,' '    "bin/check-new": "not-replayable: reads prod",'
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect string_valued_addition_fails 1 'bin/check-new'
+
+fresh
+add_after '"bin/check-a": _SINCE,' "    'bin/check-new': _TREE,"
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect single_quoted_key_fails 1 'bin/check-new'
+
+fresh
+add_after '"bin/check-a": _SINCE,' '    "bin/check-new": _SINCE,  # replay-spec-ok:'
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect exempt_marker_empty_reason_fails 1 'bin/check-new'
+
+# ---- cases that must pass (exit 0) ----
+
+fresh
+printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# gate-backtest-argv: --since={base}' > "$R/bin/check-new"
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect header_only_gate_passes 0
+
+fresh
+awk '{ sub(/"bin\/check-a": _SINCE,/, "\"bin/check-a\": _TREE,"); print }' "$R/$GB" > "$R/$GB.new"
+mv "$R/$GB.new" "$R/$GB"
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect value_edit_passes 0
+
+fresh
+add_after '"bin/check-a": _SINCE,' '    # "bin/check-new": _SINCE,'
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect comment_line_passes 0
+
+fresh
+awk '!/bin\/check-b/' "$R/$GB" > "$R/$GB.new"
+mv "$R/$GB.new" "$R/$GB"
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect removal_passes 0
+
+fresh
+awk '
+    /"bin\/check-c": ReplaySpec\(/ { print "    \"bin/check-c\": _SINCE,"; skip = 1; next }
+    skip && /^    \),/ { skip = 0; next }
+    skip { next }
+    { print }
+' "$R/$GB" > "$R/$GB.new"
+mv "$R/$GB.new" "$R/$GB"
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect reformat_passes 0
+
+fresh
+add_after '"bin/check-z": 1,' '    "bin/check-y": 2,'
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect other_dict_key_passes 0
+
+fresh
+add_after '"bin/check-a": _SINCE,' '    "bin/check-new": _SINCE,  # replay-spec-ok: needs timeout field'
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect exempt_marker_passes 0
+
+# ---- error paths (exit 2) ----
+
+fresh
+awk '{ sub(/REPLAY_SPECS/, "REPLAY_TABLE"); print }' "$R/$GB" > "$R/$GB.new"
+mv "$R/$GB.new" "$R/$GB"
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=$BASE"
+expect missing_block_errors 2 'no REPLAY_SPECS block'
+
+fresh
+usage_ok=1
+run_with "$CHK"
+[ "$RC" = 2 ] || usage_ok=0
+run_with "$CHK" --since "$BASE"
+[ "$RC" = 2 ] || usage_ok=0
+run_with "$CHK" "--since=nosuchref"
+[ "$RC" = 2 ] || usage_ok=0
+if [ "$usage_ok" = 1 ]; then
+    pass usage_errors
+else
+    fail "usage_errors (a bad invocation did not exit 2)"
+fi
+
+# ---- mutation proof ----
+
+fresh
+add_after '"bin/check-a": _SINCE,' '    "bin/check-new": _SINCE,'
+MUT="$T/mutated"
+sed -E 's/comm -13 /comm -12 /' "$CHK" > "$MUT"
+chmod +x "$MUT"
+if cmp -s "$CHK" "$MUT"; then
+    fail "mutation_proof (the sed mutation did not change the check)"
+else
+    # comm -12 lists the keys both sides share, so the mutated gate flags the old keys and
+    # never names the added one. The real gate names it (case added_key_fails).
+    run_with "$MUT" "--since=$BASE"
+    if grep -qF -- 'bin/check-new' <<< "$OUT"; then
+        fail "mutation_proof (the mutated gate still names the added key: $OUT)"
+    else
+        pass mutation_proof
+    fi
+fi
+
+echo ""
+echo "$PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
+[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# bin/jsb-parity-watch — hourly zero-token watcher for the JSB parity loop.
+#
+# Run by the com.ibl5.jsb-parity-watch LaunchAgent (bin/jsb-parity-watch-setup).
+# It reads the parity ledger and GitHub PR state, picks one verdict per in-flight
+# ledger row, computes every verdict first, then acts once per run:
+#
+#   row state                                         verdict
+#   ------------------------------------------------  ------------------------------
+#   PR merged                                         FIRE webhook
+#   PR closed without merge                           FIRE webhook
+#   PR open, a check failed (new head SHA)            FIRE webhook (once per SHA)
+#   PR open, checks pending                           wait
+#   PR open, green, auto-merge armed                  wait
+#   PR open, green, auto-merge not armed              STALL (DM: held for owner)
+#   no PR, plan queued, automouse idle                KICK (schedule a run)
+#   no PR, plan queued, automouse running             wait
+#   no PR, a loaded plan-now job may own the slug     wait
+#   no PR, plan in done/ or skipped/                  STALL (DM)
+#   no PR, failure report names the slug              STALL (DM)
+#   no PR, nothing found                              STALL (DM: no trace)
+#   no row in flight                                  FIRE webhook
+#
+# One webhook POST, one automouse kick and one DM per new stall key per run.
+# A gh failure on any row aborts the run before any action. Any unexpected error
+# logs one line and exits 0, so launchd never throttles the job.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   bin/jsb-parity-watch             # act
+#   bin/jsb-parity-watch --dry-run   # print config, row and decision lines; act on nothing
+#
+# Env seams (all optional; empty means the default): JSB_WATCH_PARITY_DIR,
+# JSB_WATCH_BIN, JSB_WATCH_PLANNOW_DIR, JSB_WATCH_NOW (epoch seconds).
+#
+# The watcher writes only under $HOME/.cache. It never writes under the parity
+# dir, never runs parity_loop.py, and calls gh only as `pr list`.
+set -Eeuo pipefail
+export PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/opt/mariadb/bin:$HOME/.bun/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
+
+log() { printf '%s jsb-parity-watch: %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*"; }
+trap 'log "error at line $LINENO; no action taken"; exit 0' ERR
+
+SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+REPO_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."
+# shellcheck source=bin/lib/launchd-sched.sh
+. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/launchd-sched.sh"
+MAIN_WT="$(lsched_main_wt "$REPO_ROOT")"
+
+STALE_AGE_S=14400
+MUTEX_STALE_S=60
+REFIRE_S=21600
+SCHEDULE_DELAY_S=120
+FAILED_CONCLUSIONS='["FAILURE","CANCELLED","TIMED_OUT","ACTION_REQUIRED","STARTUP_FAILURE","ERROR"]'
+INFLIGHT_FILTER='.rows[] | select(.status == "captured" and (.plan_slug // "") != "") | "\(.id) \(.plan_slug)"'
+PR_PICK='(map(select(.state == "OPEN")) + map(select(.state == "MERGED")) + map(select(.state == "CLOSED")))[0] // empty'
+CHECK_FILTER='[.statusCheckRollup[]? | ((.conclusion // .state // "") | ascii_upcase) as $c | (.status // "COMPLETED") as $s | if any($failed[]; . == $c) then "failed" elif ($s != "COMPLETED" or $c == "" or $c == "PENDING" or $c == "EXPECTED") then "pending" else "green" end] | if any(.[]; . == "failed") then "failed" elif (length == 0 or any(.[]; . == "pending")) then "pending" else "green" end'
+PARITY_DIR="${JSB_WATCH_PARITY_DIR:-$MAIN_WT/jsb-native/parity}"
+JSB_BIN="${JSB_WATCH_BIN:-$SCRIPT_DIR}"
+PLANNOW_DIR="${JSB_WATCH_PLANNOW_DIR:-/tmp}"
+NOW="${JSB_WATCH_NOW:-$(date +%s)}"
+case "$NOW" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "jsb-parity-watch: JSB_WATCH_NOW must be epoch seconds" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
+CACHE_DIR="$HOME/.cache"
+FIRED_SHAS="$CACHE_DIR/jsb-parity-watch.fired-shas"
+STALLS="$CACHE_DIR/jsb-parity-stalls.txt"
+LAST="$CACHE_DIR/jsb-parity-watch.last"
+WEBHOOK_FILE="$HOME/.config/jsb-parity/webhook-url"
+AUTOMOUSE_DIR="$HOME/.claude/projects/-Users-ajaynicolas-GitHub-IBL5/automouse"
+
+DRY_RUN=0
+FIRE_REASONS=""
+STALL_KEYS=""
+KICK=0
+GH_ERROR=""
+FACTS=""
+ROW_LINES=""
+fp=""
+
+usage() {
+    cat <<'USAGE'
+Usage: bin/jsb-parity-watch [--dry-run]
+  --dry-run   print config, row and decision lines; take no action
+  -h, --help  show this help
+USAGE
+}
+
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+    case "$1" in
+        --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
+        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+        *) echo "jsb-parity-watch: unknown argument: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+    esac
+done
+
+quiet_exit() { log "$1"; exit 0; }
+
+# dry_guard <action>: returns 0 when the action may run, 1 (after saying so) in dry-run.
+dry_guard() {
+    [ "$DRY_RUN" = 0 ] || { echo "dry-run: would $1"; return 1; }
+}
+
+fmt_epoch() {
+    if date -d @0 +%s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        date -d "@$1" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'
+    else
+        date -r "$1" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'
+    fi
+}
+
+sha256_of() {
+    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
+    else
+        shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
+    fi
+}
+
+# match_plan <dir> <slug>: print the basename of the first plan file for the slug.
+# A dangling queue symlink counts.
+match_plan() {
+    local dir="$1" slug="$2" f
+    for f in "$dir/$slug.md" "$dir"/*-"$slug".md; do
+        if [ -e "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ]; then
+            basename "$f"
+            return 0
+        fi
+    done
+    return 0
+}
+
+# lock_is_stale <lockdir>: returns 0 when stale. Mirrors
+# jsb-native/tools/parity_loop/lock.py in the main checkout.
+lock_is_stale() {
+    local lockdir="$1" pid="" epoch="" host="" mtime
+    if [ -r "$lockdir/pid" ]; then
+        read -r pid epoch host < "$lockdir/pid" || true
+        case "$pid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) pid="" ;; esac
+        case "$epoch" in ''|*[!0-9]*) pid="" ;; esac
+    fi
+    if [ -n "$pid" ]; then
+        if [ "$pid" -gt 0 ] && ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then return 0; fi
+        if [ $((NOW - epoch)) -gt "$STALE_AGE_S" ]; then return 0; fi
+        return 1
+    fi
+    mtime=$(stat -c %Y "$lockdir" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m "$lockdir" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
+    if [ $((NOW - mtime)) -gt "$MUTEX_STALE_S" ]; then return 0; fi
+    return 1
+}
+
+# row_verdict <id> <slug>: line 1 is the verdict; line 2 is the fingerprint fact
+# (absent when the row has no PR).
+row_verdict() {
+    local id="$1" slug="$2" prs pr state number sha check armed f b log label newest r slug_re
+    # Runs in a command-substitution subshell. The inherited ERR trap would print its
+    # log line into the captured output and exit 0, which hides a failed gh or jq call.
+    # Cleared here, a failure exits the subshell non-zero and main's own trap handles it.
+    trap - ERR
+    slug_re="${slug}([^A-Za-z0-9]|\$)"
+    if ! prs=$(gh pr list --repo a-jay85/IBL5 --head "$slug" --state all --json number,state,mergedAt,url,autoMergeRequest,statusCheckRollup,headRefOid 2>/dev/null) \
+        || ! pr=$(printf '%s' "$prs" | jq -c "$PR_PICK" 2>/dev/null); then
+        echo "ERROR:gh"; return 0
+    fi
+
+    if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
+        state=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r '.state')
+        number=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r '.number')
+        sha=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r '.headRefOid // ""')
+        check="-"
+        case "$state" in
+            MERGED) echo "FIRE:merged" ;;
+            CLOSED) echo "FIRE:closed" ;;
+            OPEN)
+                check=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r --argjson failed "$FAILED_CONCLUSIONS" "$CHECK_FILTER")
+                armed=$(printf '%s' "$pr" | jq -r 'if .autoMergeRequest == null then "no" else "yes" end')
+                case "$check" in
+                    failed) if grep -qxF -- "$id:$sha" "$FIRED_SHAS" 2>/dev/null; then echo "WAIT:check-failed-seen"; else echo "FIRE:check-failed:$sha"; fi ;;
+                    pending) echo "WAIT:checks-pending" ;;
+                    green) if [ "$armed" = "yes" ]; then echo "WAIT:auto-merge-armed"; else echo "STALL:held-for-owner:$number"; fi ;;
+                    *) echo "WAIT:check-unknown" ;;
+                esac ;;
+            *) echo "WAIT:pr-state-unknown" ;;
+        esac
+        printf '%s=%s:%s:%s:%s\n' "$id" "$number" "$state" "$sha" "$check"
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    f=$(match_plan "$AUTOMOUSE_DIR/queue" "$slug")
+    if [ -n "$f" ]; then
+        if pgrep -f 'bin/automouse/run' >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "WAIT:automouse-running"; else echo "KICK:schedule"; fi
+        return 0
+    fi
+
+    for label in $(launchctl list 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'com\.ibl5\.plan-now-[0-9-]+' || true); do
+        log="$PLANNOW_DIR/plan-now-${label#com.ibl5.plan-now-}.log"
+        if grep -qE "$slug_re" "$log" 2>/dev/null; then
+            echo "WAIT:plan-now-running"; return 0
+        fi
+        if [ ! -f "$log" ] || ! grep -qE 'jsb-port-' "$log"; then echo "WAIT:plan-now-unattributed"; return 0; fi
+    done
+
+    f=$(match_plan "$AUTOMOUSE_DIR/done" "$slug")
+    if [ -n "$f" ]; then echo "STALL:plan-done:$f"; return 0; fi
+    f=$(match_plan "$AUTOMOUSE_DIR/skipped" "$slug")
+    if [ -n "$f" ]; then echo "STALL:plan-skipped:$f"; return 0; fi
+
+    for r in "$AUTOMOUSE_DIR"/reports/*"$slug"*; do
+        [ -e "$r" ] || continue
+        b=$(basename "$r")
+        case "$b" in *-done-*) continue ;; esac
+        grep -qE "$slug_re" <<< "$b" || continue
+        echo "STALL:plan-failed:$b"; return 0
+    done
+
+    newest=""
+    for f in "$PLANNOW_DIR"/plan-now-*.log; do
+        [ -e "$f" ] || continue
+        if grep -qE "$slug_re" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then newest="$f"; fi
+    done
+    if [ -n "$newest" ]; then
+        echo "STALL:no-trace:$(basename "$newest")"
+    else
+        echo "STALL:no-trace:none"
+    fi
+    return 0
+}
+
+# stall_message <key>: the DM text for one stall key (<id>:<stage>:<ref>).
+stall_message() {
+    local key="$1" id rest stage ref slug
+    id="${key%%:*}"; rest="${key#*:}"; stage="${rest%%:*}"; ref="${rest#*:}"
+    slug=$(jq -r --arg id "$id" '[.rows[] | select(.id == $id) | .plan_slug][0] // ""' "$PARITY_DIR/ledger.json" || echo "")
+    case "$stage" in
+        held-for-owner)
+            printf 'JSB parity watch: %s (%s) has PR https://github.com/a-jay85/IBL5/pull/%s. It is green and auto-merge is not armed.\n' "$id" "$slug" "$ref" ;;
+        plan-done)
+            printf 'JSB parity watch: %s (%s) has no PR, but its plan is in done/: %s.\n' "$id" "$slug" "$ref" ;;
+        plan-skipped)
+            printf 'JSB parity watch: %s (%s) has no PR, but its plan is in skipped/: %s.\n' "$id" "$slug" "$ref" ;;
+        plan-failed)
+            printf 'JSB parity watch: %s (%s) has no PR and a failure report names it: %s.\n' "$id" "$slug" "$ref" ;;
+        no-trace)
+            if [ "$ref" = "none" ]; then
+                printf 'JSB parity watch: %s (%s) has no PR, no queued plan and no plan-now log naming it.\n' "$id" "$slug"
+            else
+                printf 'JSB parity watch: %s (%s) has no PR and no queued plan. Newest plan-now log naming it is %s:\n%s\n' \
+                    "$id" "$slug" "$ref" "$(tail -n 5 "$PLANNOW_DIR/$ref" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+            fi ;;
+        *)
+            printf 'JSB parity watch: %s (%s) is stalled (%s).\n' "$id" "$slug" "$key" ;;
+    esac
+}
+
+# fire_webhook <reasons>: POST once. The URL goes to curl only through its stdin config.
+fire_webhook() {
+    local reasons="$1" url body code r
+    dry_guard "fire webhook ($reasons)" || return 0
+    url=$(head -n 1 "$WEBHOOK_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    case "$url" in
+        https://*) ;;
+        *) log "webhook file unusable; no action taken"; return 0 ;;
+    esac
+    case "$url" in
+        *'"'*) log "webhook file unusable; no action taken"; return 0 ;;
+    esac
+    body='{"source":"jsb-parity-watch","reasons":"'"$reasons"'"}'
+    code=$(printf 'url = "%s"\n' "$url" | curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data "$body" -K - 2>/dev/null) || code=000
+    case "$code" in [0-9][0-9][0-9]) ;; *) code=000 ;; esac
+    case "$code" in 2??) ;; *) log "webhook POST failed (HTTP $code)"; return 0 ;; esac
+    mkdir -p "$CACHE_DIR"
+    printf '%s %s\n' "$fp" "$NOW" > "$LAST.tmp"
+    mv "$LAST.tmp" "$LAST"
+    for r in $reasons; do
+        case "$r" in
+            *:check-failed:*) printf '%s:%s\n' "${r%%:*}" "${r##*:}" >> "$FIRED_SHAS" ;;
+        esac
+    done
+    log "webhook POST ok (HTTP $code) reasons=$reasons"
+}
+
+main() {
+    local lockdir ledger inflight recording id slug out verdict fact key msg when last_fp="" last_at=0
+
+    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
+        echo "config: parity_dir=$PARITY_DIR bin=$JSB_BIN plannow_dir=$PLANNOW_DIR now=$NOW"
+    fi
+
+    lockdir="$PARITY_DIR/state/loop.lock"
+    if [ -d "$lockdir" ]; then
+        if ! lock_is_stale "$lockdir"; then
+            quiet_exit "run lock held; no action taken"
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    ledger="$PARITY_DIR/ledger.json"
+    if [ ! -f "$ledger" ]; then
+        quiet_exit "ledger missing at $ledger; no action taken"
+    fi
+    if ! jq -e '.rows | type == "array"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        quiet_exit "ledger unreadable at $ledger; no action taken"
+    fi
+    inflight=$(jq -r "$INFLIGHT_FILTER" "$ledger")
+    recording="none"
+    if [ -f "$PARITY_DIR/recordings/index.json" ]; then
+        recording=$(jq -r '.current // "none"' "$PARITY_DIR/recordings/index.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "none")
+    fi
+
+    while read -r id slug; do
+        [ -n "$id" ] || continue
+        out=$(row_verdict "$id" "$slug")
+        verdict="${out%%$'\n'*}"
+        case "$verdict" in
+            ERROR:*|FIRE:*|KICK:*|STALL:*|WAIT:*) ;;
+            *) quiet_exit "no verdict for $id; no action taken" ;;
+        esac
+        case "$out" in
+            *$'\n'*) fact="${out#*$'\n'}"; fact="${fact%%$'\n'*}" ;;
+            *) fact="" ;;
+        esac
+        [ -n "$fact" ] || fact="$id=none"
+        ROW_LINES="${ROW_LINES}row $id $slug $verdict"$'\n'
+        FACTS="${FACTS:+$FACTS,}$fact"
+        case "$verdict" in
+            ERROR:*) GH_ERROR="$slug" ;;
+            FIRE:*) FIRE_REASONS="${FIRE_REASONS:+$FIRE_REASONS }$id:${verdict#FIRE:}" ;;
+            KICK:*) KICK=1 ;;
+            STALL:*) STALL_KEYS="${STALL_KEYS:+$STALL_KEYS }$id:${verdict#STALL:}" ;;
+            WAIT:*) ;;
+        esac
+    done <<< "$inflight"
+
+    if [ -n "$GH_ERROR" ]; then
+        quiet_exit "gh pr list failed for $GH_ERROR; no action taken"
+    fi
+    if [ -z "$inflight" ]; then FIRE_REASONS="no-row-in-flight"; fi
+
+    printf '%s' "$ROW_LINES"
+
+    if [ "$KICK" = 1 ]; then
+        if dry_guard "schedule an automouse run"; then
+            when=$(fmt_epoch $((NOW + SCHEDULE_DELAY_S)))
+            log "scheduling automouse run at $when"
+            "$JSB_BIN/automouse/run" schedule "$when" >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "automouse schedule failed"
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    for key in $STALL_KEYS; do
+        if grep -qxF -- "$key" "$STALLS" 2>/dev/null; then
+            continue
+        fi
+        if dry_guard "send stall DM $key"; then
+            msg=$(stall_message "$key")
+            if printf '%s' "$msg" | "$JSB_BIN/discord-dm" --quiet - >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+                mkdir -p "$CACHE_DIR"
+                printf '%s\n' "$key" >> "$STALLS"
+            else
+                log "discord-dm failed for $key; will retry next run"
+            fi
+        fi
+    done
+
+    if [ -z "$FIRE_REASONS" ]; then
+        echo "decision: no fire"
+        return 0
+    fi
+    fp="$(sha256_of "$ledger")|${recording// /_}|$FACTS"
+    if [ -f "$LAST" ]; then
+        read -r last_fp last_at < "$LAST" || true
+    fi
+    case "$last_at" in ''|*[!0-9]*) last_at=0 ;; esac
+    if [ "$fp" = "$last_fp" ] && [ $((NOW - last_at)) -lt "$REFIRE_S" ]; then
+        echo "decision: fire suppressed (unchanged state, last fire $((NOW - last_at))s ago)"
+        return 0
+    fi
+    echo "decision: fire ($FIRE_REASONS)"
+    fire_webhook "$FIRE_REASONS"
+}
+
+main

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# bin/jsb-parity-watch-setup — install the hourly LaunchAgent for bin/jsb-parity-watch.
+#
+# Installs com.ibl5.jsb-parity-watch: StartInterval 3600 plus RunAtLoad. The job
+# always points at the durable MAIN checkout's bin/jsb-parity-watch, so this script
+# installs from any checkout, worktrees included. Until the watcher exists in the
+# main checkout (it appears when its PR merges), ProgramArguments wraps the path in
+# a `test -x ... || exit 0` guard, so each run exits 0 and launchd logs no failure.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   bin/jsb-parity-watch-setup                    install (or replace) and load the LaunchAgent
+#   bin/jsb-parity-watch-setup --print-schedule   print the plist to stdout; no side effect
+#   bin/jsb-parity-watch-setup --uninstall        unload and remove the LaunchAgent
+#
+# Environment: HOME (required). MAIN_WT overrides the main checkout (tests only).
+set -euo pipefail
+
+REPO_ROOT="${REPO_ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)}"
+# Script-relative: tests point REPO_ROOT at a fake tree, so do not source via it.
+# shellcheck source=bin/lib/launchd-sched.sh
+. "$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/lib/launchd-sched.sh"
+
+usage() {
+    awk 'NR==1{next} /^# ?---$/{exit} /^#/{sub(/^# ?/,"");print;next} {exit}' "$0"
+}
+
+ACTION="install"
+SEEN=0
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+    case "$SEEN:$1" in
+        0:--print-schedule) ACTION="print" ;;
+        0:--uninstall) ACTION="uninstall" ;;
+        0:-h|0:--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+        *) echo "jsb-parity-watch-setup: unknown argument: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+    esac
+    SEEN=1
+    shift
+done
+
+[ -n "${MAIN_WT:-}" ] || MAIN_WT="$(lsched_main_wt "$REPO_ROOT")"
+LABEL="com.ibl5.jsb-parity-watch"
+LOG_DIR="$HOME/Library/Logs"
+PLIST_PATH="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/$LABEL.plist"
+PROGRAM="$MAIN_WT/bin/jsb-parity-watch"
+WRAPPER="test -x '$PROGRAM' || exit 0; exec '$PROGRAM'"
+
+# Single source of truth for the plist, used by --print-schedule and install.
+plist_body() {
+    lsched_key_string Label "$LABEL"
+    lsched_program_arguments /bin/sh -c "$WRAPPER"
+    lsched_key_string WorkingDirectory "$MAIN_WT"
+    lsched_key_integer StartInterval 3600
+    lsched_key_bool RunAtLoad true
+    lsched_env_open
+    # launchd starts agents with a minimal PATH. gh, jq and curl live under
+    # /opt/homebrew/bin. launchd never expands variable references, so every value
+    # here is already expanded.
+    lsched_key_string PATH "${MAIN_WT}/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:${HOME}/.local/bin" 2
+    lsched_key_string HOME "${HOME}" 2
+    lsched_env_close
+    lsched_key_string StandardOutPath "${LOG_DIR}/jsb-parity-watch.log"
+    lsched_key_string StandardErrorPath "${LOG_DIR}/jsb-parity-watch.log"
+}
+
+case "$ACTION" in
+    print)
+        lsched_plist plist_body
+        ;;
+    install)
+        if [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
+            echo "Error: HOME is unset; cannot generate a valid plist." >&2
+            exit 1
+        fi
+        lsched_install "$LABEL" "$PLIST_PATH" plist_body "$LOG_DIR"
+        echo "Installed $LABEL (StartInterval 3600, RunAtLoad). Program: $PROGRAM"
+        if [ ! -x "$PROGRAM" ]; then
+            echo "Note: $PROGRAM appears when the PR merges; until then each run exits 0."
+        fi
+        ;;
+    uninstall)
+        lsched_uninstall "$LABEL" "$PLIST_PATH"
+        echo "Removed $LABEL."
+        ;;
+esac

+. "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/harness.sh"
+
+REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+h_tmp T
+
+BASE=1795430000
+SECRET="https://hooks.example.invalid/T3-SECRET-7f3a9c"
+AMDIR=".claude/projects/-Users-ajaynicolas-GitHub-IBL5/automouse"
+
+GREEN='[{"__typename":"CheckRun","status":"COMPLETED","conclusion":"SUCCESS","name":"a"}]'
+ROLL_FAILED='[{"__typename":"CheckRun","status":"COMPLETED","conclusion":"FAILURE","name":"a"}]'
+PENDING='[{"__typename":"CheckRun","status":"IN_PROGRESS","conclusion":"","name":"a"},{"__typename":"StatusContext","context":"x","state":"EXPECTED"}]'
+NEAR_MISS='[{"__typename":"CheckRun","status":"COMPLETED","conclusion":"SKIPPED","name":"a"},{"__typename":"CheckRun","status":"COMPLETED","conclusion":"NEUTRAL","name":"b"},{"__typename":"CheckRun","status":"COMPLETED","conclusion":"SUCCESS","name":"c"}]'
+ERROR_CTX='[{"__typename":"StatusContext","context":"ci","state":"ERROR"}]'
+
+S=""
+
+# --- Sandbox ---------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# ledger <id:status:slug>...: write the sandbox ledger.
+ledger() {
+    local out='[]' t id st sl
+    for t in "$@"; do
+        id="${t%%:*}"; t="${t#*:}"; st="${t%%:*}"; sl="${t#*:}"
+        out=$(jq -c --arg id "$id" --arg st "$st" --arg sl "$sl" \
+            '. + [{id: $id, status: $st, plan_slug: (if $sl == "" then null else $sl end)}]' <<< "$out")
+    done

+}
+
+write_stub() {

+    cat > "$S/stub/$name"
+    chmod 755 "$S/stub/$name"
+}
+
+# sandbox <name>: build $S for one case, with one row (pl-0001) in flight.
+sandbox() {
+    S="$T/$1"
+    mkdir -p "$S/home/.config/jsb-parity" "$S/home/$AMDIR/queue" "$S/home/$AMDIR/done" \
+        "$S/home/$AMDIR/skipped" "$S/home/$AMDIR/reports" "$S/parity/recordings" \
+        "$S/parity/state" "$S/plannow" "$S/stub" "$S/bin/automouse" "$S/log" "$S/fix" "$S/main"
+    printf '%s\n' "$SECRET" > "$S/home/.config/jsb-parity/webhook-url"
+    chmod 600 "$S/home/.config/jsb-parity/webhook-url"
+    printf '{"current":"rec-1"}\n' > "$S/parity/recordings/index.json"
+    ledger "pl-0001:captured:jsb-port-pl-0001"
+

+#!/bin/sh

+[ -e "$JSB_STUB_DIR/fix/gh-fail" ] && exit 1

+# run_watch [args...]: run the watcher in the sandbox. Env seams default to the
+# sandbox when unset and pass through unchanged when empty ("VAR= run_watch").
+run_watch() {

+        JSB_WATCH_PARITY_DIR="${JSB_WATCH_PARITY_DIR-$S/parity}" \

+# gh_pr <slug> <number> <state> <armed yes|no> <sha> <rollup-json>
+gh_pr() {

+           url: ("https://github.com/a-jay85/IBL5/pull/" + ($n | tostring)),
+           autoMergeRequest: (if $armed == "yes" then {enabledAt: "2026-11-22T00:00:00Z", mergeMethod: "SQUASH"} else null end),

+
+main_checkout() { git -C "$REPO" worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree / && !f {print $2; f=1}'; }
+
+case_env_empty_parity_dir() {
+    sandbox env_parity
+    JSB_WATCH_PARITY_DIR='' run_watch --dry-run
+    h_eq "empty parity dir falls back to the main checkout" "$(main_checkout)/jsb-native/parity" "$(config_value parity_dir)"
+}
+
+case_env_empty_bin() {
+    sandbox env_bin
+    JSB_WATCH_BIN='' run_watch --dry-run
+    h_eq "empty bin falls back to the script dir" "$REPO/bin" "$(config_value bin)"
+}
+
+case_env_empty_plannow_dir() {
+    sandbox env_plannow
+    JSB_WATCH_PLANNOW_DIR='' run_watch --dry-run
+    h_eq "empty plan-now dir falls back to /tmp" "/tmp" "$(config_value plannow_dir)"
+}
+
+case_env_empty_now() {
+    local got real diff
+    sandbox env_now
+    JSB_WATCH_NOW='' run_watch --dry-run
+    got=$(config_value now)
+    real=$(date +%s)
+    case "$got" in
+        ''|*[!0-9]*) h_fail "empty now falls back to the clock" "got [$got]"; return 0 ;;
+    esac
+    diff=$((real - got))
+    if [ "$diff" -lt 0 ]; then diff=$((0 - diff)); fi
+    if [ "$diff" -le 5 ]; then h_pass "empty now falls back to the clock"; else h_fail "empty now falls back to the clock" "off by ${diff}s"; fi
+}
+
+case_env_invalid_now() {
+    sandbox env_bad_now
+    JSB_WATCH_NOW=abc run_watch
+    rc_is "invalid now: exit 2" 2
+    h_contains "invalid now: usage message" "$(slurp "$S/err")" "epoch seconds"
+}
+
+# --- Installer cases (rows 40-49) ---------------------------------------------------
+
+# plist_get <file> <python expression over d>
+plist_get() {
+    python3 -I -c 'import plistlib, sys; d = plistlib.load(open(sys.argv[1], "rb")); print(eval(sys.argv[2]))' "$1" "$2"
+}
+
+PLIST_NAME="com.ibl5.jsb-parity-watch.plist"
+
+case_setup_print_schedule() {
+    sandbox setup_print
+    run_setup --print-schedule
+    rc_is "print-schedule: exit 0" 0
+    cp "$S/out" "$S/print.plist"
+    h_eq "label" "com.ibl5.jsb-parity-watch" "$(plist_get "$S/print.plist" 'd["Label"]')"
+    h_eq "StartInterval" 3600 "$(plist_get "$S/print.plist" 'd["StartInterval"]')"
+    h_eq "RunAtLoad" True "$(plist_get "$S/print.plist" 'd["RunAtLoad"]')"
+    h_contains "wrapper points at the main checkout" "$(plist_get "$S/print.plist" 'd["ProgramArguments"][2]')" "$S/main/bin/jsb-parity-watch"
+    h_eq "log path" "$S/home/Library/Logs/jsb-parity-watch.log" "$(plist_get "$S/print.plist" 'd["StandardOutPath"]')"
+    h_absent "no plist written" "$S/home/Library/LaunchAgents/$PLIST_NAME"
+    h_absent "launchctl never called" "$S/log/launchctl.argv"
+}
+
+case_setup_plist_no_empty_string() {
+    sandbox setup_empty
+    run_setup --print-schedule
+    h_not_contains "no empty string element" "$(out)" "<string></string>"
+}
+
+case_setup_plist_no_unexpanded_var() {
+    local hits
+    sandbox setup_var
+    run_setup --print-schedule
+    hits=$(grep -cE '\$(\{|[A-Za-z_])' "$S/out" || true)
+    h_eq "no unexpanded variable reference" 0 "$hits"
+}
+
+case_setup_install_idempotent() {
+    local a b
+    sandbox setup_install
+    run_setup
+    rc_is "first install: exit 0" 0
+    a=$(cksum < "$S/home/Library/LaunchAgents/$PLIST_NAME")
+    run_setup
+    rc_is "second install: exit 0" 0
+    b=$(cksum < "$S/home/Library/LaunchAgents/$PLIST_NAME")
+    h_eq "plist is byte-identical after the second install" "$a" "$b"
+    h_eq "a bootstrap per run" 2 "$(grep -c '^bootstrap' "$S/log/launchctl.argv")"
+    h_contains "install notes that the program is not there yet" "$(out)" "appears when the PR merges"
+}
+
+case_setup_uninstall_idempotent() {
+    sandbox setup_uninstall
+    run_setup
+    h_exists "installed first" "$S/home/Library/LaunchAgents/$PLIST_NAME"
+    run_setup --uninstall
+    rc_is "first uninstall: exit 0" 0
+    run_setup --uninstall
+    rc_is "second uninstall: exit 0" 0
+    h_absent "plist removed" "$S/home/Library/LaunchAgents/$PLIST_NAME"
+}
+
+case_setup_from_worktree_points_main() {
+    sandbox setup_worktree
+    mkdir -p "$S/wt"
+    SETUP_REPO_ROOT="$S/wt" run_setup
+    rc_is "install from a worktree: exit 0" 0
+    h_contains "wrapper names the main checkout" "$(plist_get "$S/home/Library/LaunchAgents/$PLIST_NAME" 'd["ProgramArguments"][2]')" "$S/main/bin/jsb-parity-watch"
+    h_not_contains "wrapper never names the worktree" "$(plist_get "$S/home/Library/LaunchAgents/$PLIST_NAME" 'd["ProgramArguments"][2]')" "$S/wt"
+}
+
+case_setup_wrapper_missing_target() {
+    local w rc
+    sandbox setup_wrapper
+    run_setup --print-schedule
+    cp "$S/out" "$S/print.plist"
+    w=$(plist_get "$S/print.plist" 'd["ProgramArguments"][2]')
+    /bin/sh -c "$w"
+    rc=$?
+    h_eq "missing program: wrapper exits 0" 0 "$rc"
+    mkdir -p "$S/main/bin"
+    printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 3\n' > "$S/main/bin/jsb-parity-watch"
+    chmod 755 "$S/main/bin/jsb-parity-watch"
+    /bin/sh -c "$w"
+    rc=$?
+    h_eq "present program: wrapper passes its exit code through" 3 "$rc"
+}
+
+case_setup_unknown_flag_rejected() {
+    local a
+    sandbox setup_flag
+    for a in --bogus --uninstall=1; do
+        run_setup "$a"
+        rc_is "$a: exit 2" 2
+        h_contains "$a: stderr says so" "$(slurp "$S/err")" "unknown argument"
+        h_absent "$a: no plist written" "$S/home/Library/LaunchAgents/$PLIST_NAME"
+    done
+    run_setup --print-schedule --uninstall
+    rc_is "a second argument: exit 2" 2
+}
+
+case_setup_main_wt_empty() {
+    sandbox setup_main_empty
+    SETUP_MAIN_WT='' run_setup --print-schedule
+    cp "$S/out" "$S/print.plist"
+    h_contains "empty MAIN_WT falls back to the first worktree" "$(plist_get "$S/print.plist" 'd["ProgramArguments"][2]')" "$(main_checkout)/bin/jsb-parity-watch"
+    # An unset MAIN_WT falls back the same way. A guard written as ${MAIN_WT+set}
+    # would keep the empty value above, so the first assertion would fail.
+    env -u MAIN_WT HOME="$S/home" REPO_ROOT="$REPO" "$REPO/bin/jsb-parity-watch-setup" --print-schedule > "$S/print-unset.plist" 2> "$S/err"
+    h_contains "unset MAIN_WT falls back to the first worktree" "$(plist_get "$S/print-unset.plist" 'd["ProgramArguments"][2]')" "$(main_checkout)/bin/jsb-parity-watch"
+}
+
+# --- Dispatch ------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+ALL_CASES=""
+while read -r _ _ fn; do
+    case "$fn" in
+        case_*) ALL_CASES="$ALL_CASES $fn" ;;
+    esac
+done < <(declare -F)
+
+if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then
+    CASES="$*"
+else
+    CASES="$ALL_CASES"
+fi
+
+for c in $CASES; do
+    case "$ALL_CASES " in
+        *" $c "*) "$c" ;;
+        *) h_fail "unknown case: $c" ;;
+    esac
+done
+
+h_done

+#!/bin/bash
+# <!-- no-adr: additive lint gate over bin/ agent permission flags; ADR-0093 already owns the agent trust boundary this gate checks -->
+# bin/check-agent-allowlist — CI gate: a headless claude run under bin/ must not
+# get a wider grant than its comments document.
+#
+# Why: PR #3379 shipped bin/sim-recap-tick with an auto-approving permission
+# mode and an allow rule for the raw mysql client, which can run shell commands
+# through `system` and `\!`. Review caught it three times (backlog issue 1609).
+# This gate fails the PR that adds such a grant without a documented reason.
+#
+# Usage: bin/check-agent-allowlist   (scans the repo that holds this script)
+# gate-backtest-argv:
+# ---
+# A finding is accepted by a comment `# agent-allowlist-ok: <reason>` whose
+# reason is 15+ chars, on the flagged line itself or in the unbroken comment
+# block directly above the first line of the backslash-continued command.
+# ---
+# Fail closed: not a git repo, a git error, or no tracked bin/ files exits 2.
+PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin${PATH:+:$PATH}"; export PATH
+
+usage() {
+    cat <<'EOF'
+Usage: bin/check-agent-allowlist
+
+CI gate: scans tracked files under bin/ (skipping bin/test-* and *.md) for a
+headless claude run that gets
+  --permission-mode acceptEdits or bypassPermissions, or
+  an allow rule (--allowedTools / --tools) whose Bash(...) binary is a
+  shell-capable client (mysql, psql, bash, ssh, ...) or a $VARIABLE, or
+  a bare Bash, Bash(*) or Bash(*:*) rule written on the command line,
+and exits 1 unless a "# agent-allowlist-ok: <reason of 15+ chars>" comment
+sits on the line or in the unbroken comment block above the command.
+
+Exit codes:
+  0  No undocumented grant found
+  1  One or more findings (printed as path:line: kind: detail)
+  2  Usage error, not a git repo, or no tracked files under bin/
+EOF
+}
+
+die() { echo "check-agent-allowlist: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+set -eu
+
+case "${1:-}" in
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    "") ;;
+    *) usage >&2; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
+esac
+
+SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+if ! ROOT=$(git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null); then
+    die "not inside a git repo: $SCRIPT_DIR"
+fi
+if ! FILES=$(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- bin); then
+    die "git ls-files failed in $ROOT"
+fi
+[ -n "$FILES" ] || die "no tracked files under bin/ in $ROOT"
+
+AWK_PROG='
+function trim(s) { sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", s); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", s); return s }
+function marker_ok(s,   m) {
+    if (!match(s, /#[[:space:]]*agent-allowlist-ok:/)) return 0
+    m = trim(substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH))
+    return length(m) >= 15
+}
+function covered(n,   s, k) {
+    if (marker_ok(line[n])) return 1
+    s = n
+    while (s > 1 && line[s-1] ~ /\\[[:space:]]*$/) s--
+    for (k = s - 1; k >= 1 && line[k] ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/; k--)
+        if (marker_ok(line[k])) return 1
+    return 0
+}
+function report(n, kind, detail) {
+    if (!covered(n)) printf "%s:%d: %s: %s\n", path, n, kind, detail
+}
+function is_allow_flag(f) { return f ~ /^--(allowed-?[Tt]ools|tools)$/ }
+# last_flag: the last --flag word on s, or "" when s has none.
+function last_flag(s,   f) {
+    f = ""
+    while (match(s, /(^|[[:space:]])--[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*/)) {
+        f = substr(s, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", f)
+        s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+    }
+    return f
+}
+# allow_text: the text of s that follows an allow flag, minus a trailing
+# comment. on=1 means s starts inside allow context (continued statement).
+function allow_text(s, on,   out, f) {
+    sub(/[[:space:]]#.*$/, "", s)
+    out = ""
+    while (match(s, /(^|[[:space:]])--[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*/)) {
+        if (on) out = out " " substr(s, 1, RSTART - 1)
+        f = substr(s, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", f)
+        on = is_allow_flag(f)
+        s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+    }
+    if (on) out = out " " s
+    return out
+}
+# hide_flags: s with each -- inside a Bash(...) token swapped for SUBSEP
+# pairs, so allow_text does not read a --word inside a rule as a flag.
+function hide_flags(s,   out, tok) {
+    out = ""
+    while (match(s, /Bash\([^)]*\)/)) {
+        tok = substr(s, RSTART, RLENGTH)
+        gsub(/--/, SUBSEP SUBSEP, tok)
+        out = out substr(s, 1, RSTART - 1) tok
+        s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+    }
+    return out s
+}
+{ line[NR] = $0 }
+END {
+    carry = 0
+    for (n = 1; n <= NR; n++) {
+        t = line[n]
+        if (t ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/) { carry = 0; continue }
+        if (t ~ /--permission-mode[[:space:]=]+[^[:space:]]?(acceptEdits|bypassPermissions)/)
+            report(n, "permission-mode", "auto-approving mode needs an agent-allowlist-ok marker")
+        # Allow context runs from an --allowedTools/--tools flag across the
+        # backslash-continued statement until another flag starts.
+        allow = 0
+        cin = carry
+        if (t ~ /--allowed-?[Tt]ools|--tools([[:space:]=]|$)/) allow = 1
+        else if (carry && t !~ /^[[:space:]]*--[A-Za-z]/) allow = 1
+        lf = last_flag(t)
+        if (lf != "") carry = is_allow_flag(lf)
+        else carry = carry && allow
+        if (t !~ /\\[[:space:]]*$/) carry = 0
+        if (!allow) continue
+        # Scan only the allow segment, so a deny list on the same line is
+        # not read as a grant.
+        seg = allow_text(hide_flags(t), cin)
+        gsub(SUBSEP SUBSEP, "--", seg)
+        rest = seg
+        while (match(rest, /Bash\([^)]*\)/)) {
+            tok = substr(rest, RSTART, RLENGTH)
+            rest = substr(rest, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+            bin = substr(tok, 6, length(tok) - 6)
+            sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", bin)
+            sub(/[[:space:]].*$/, "", bin)
+            gsub(/"/, "", bin); gsub(sq, "", bin)
+            sub(/:?\*$/, "", bin)
+            sub(/:$/, "", bin)
+            if (bin == "" || bin == "*") {
+                report(n, "bare-bash-rule", tok " lets the agent run any shell command")
+                continue
+            }
+            if (bin ~ /^\$/) {
+                report(n, "variable-rule", tok " names its binary through a variable; show it is a safe wrapper and add a marker")
+                continue
+            }
+            sub(/^.*\//, "", bin)
+            if (bin ~ /^(mysql|mariadb|psql|sqlite3|bash|sh|zsh|env|eval|python|python3|node|perl|ruby|php|ssh)$/)
+                report(n, "shell-client-rule", tok " lets the agent run a shell-capable client")
+        }
+        # A bare Bash word after an allow flag grants every shell command.
+        # Bash(...) tokens are blanked first so their first word is not read.
+        gsub(/Bash\([^)]*\)/, " ", seg)
+        nw = split(seg, w, "[[:space:],\"" sq "=()]+")
+        for (i = 1; i <= nw; i++)
+            if (w[i] == "Bash") {
+                report(n, "bare-bash-rule", "a bare Bash rule lets the agent run any shell command")
+                break
+            }
+    }
+}'
+
+found=0
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+    case "$f" in
+        bin/test-*|bin/check-agent-allowlist|*.md) continue ;;
+    esac
+    [ -f "$ROOT/$f" ] || continue
+    grep -Iq . "$ROOT/$f" < /dev/null || continue
+    if ! out=$(awk -v path="$f" -v sq="'" "$AWK_PROG" "$ROOT/$f" < /dev/null); then
+        die "awk failed on $f"
+    fi
+    if [ -n "$out" ]; then
+        printf '%s\n' "$out"
+        found=1
+    fi
+done <<< "$FILES"
+exit "$found"

+# True when <pid> or any of its ancestors is a launchd stub PID (fixture_pid).
+# Mirrors fleet-status's pid_is_accounted_for walk, which drops a session whose
+# ancestry reaches a printed PID.
+fixture_ancestry_collides() {
+    local pid="${1:-}" hops=0
+    while [ -n "$pid" ] && [ "$pid" != "0" ] && [ "$pid" != "1" ] && [ "$hops" -lt 24 ]; do
+        fixture_pid "$pid" && { COLLIDING_PID="$pid"; return 0; }
+        pid="$(ps -o ppid= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')"
+        hops=$(( hops + 1 ))
+    done
+    return 1
+}
+
+# spawn_orphan <var> <dir> <cmd...> starts <cmd> in <dir> as a true orphan and
+# stores its PID in <var>. A throwaway subshell backgrounds the command, writes
+# its PID to a file, and exits, so the command is reparented away from this
+# script. A direct child is not enough: fleet-status walks ancestry, and on
+# Linux CI this script's own PID can equal a launchd stub row's PID (6001-6005,
+# seen in CI with orphan PIDs 6109 and 6128). The orphan then counts as that
+# row's child and leaves the orphan section. Respawns, bounded, until neither
+# the PID nor any ancestor matches a stub row.
+spawn_orphan() {
+    local var="$1" dir="$2" pidfile="$TMP/orphan.pid" try _pid=''
+    shift 2
+    COLLIDING_PID=''

+        fixture_ancestry_collides "$_pid" || break
+        kill "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
+        _pid=''
+    done
+    [ -n "$_pid" ] || printf 'WARN: %s: every spawn hit stub PID %s in its ancestry\n' \
+        "$var" "${COLLIDING_PID:-?}" >&2
+    eval "$var=\$_pid"

+#!/bin/bash
+# bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files: fails when a JSB runtime data file at
+# the ibl5/ root is git-tracked (usually force-tracked by a .gitignore "!"
+# negation) and is not on the ALLOWLIST below.
+#
+# The deploy job in .github/workflows/main.yml runs
+# `git reset --hard origin/production`, which restores every tracked file. A
+# tracked data file that the runtime or a manual upload replaced on the server
+# goes back to the stale committed copy on the next deploy. Ignored files survive.
+#
+# Scope: the extensions in JSB_EXTS, ibl5/ root only, extension case-insensitive.
+# Fixtures under ibl5/tests/ are out of scope.
+# Exits 0 (clean), 1 (tracked data file not allowlisted), 2 (usage or setup error).
+#
+# CI (tests.yml) runs it with no arguments; the script finds the repo from its own path.
+# gate-backtest-argv:
+set -euo pipefail
+
+JSB_EXTS="lge sch plr sco car trn his asw rcb awa dra ret hof plb"
+
+# One entry per line: <repo-relative path>|<why it must stay tracked>.
+# Every entry needs a reason. Prefer moving a fixture under ibl5/tests/.
+ALLOWLIST='
+ibl5/IBL5.lge|fixture for LgeFileParserTest and LeagueConfigServiceTest
+ibl5/IBL5.sch|fixture for SchFileParserTest and e2e engine-shadow-spawn-on-update
+ibl5/Olympics.sch|JsbSourceResolver disk fallback when the archive has no .sch entry'
+
+usage() {
+  cat <<'EOF'
+Usage: bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files [--repo-root=<dir>] [--help|-h]
+Fails when a JSB runtime data file at the ibl5/ root is git-tracked and not
+allowlisted in this script. --repo-root=<dir> scans another git work tree
+(the = form is required). Default: the repo holding this script.
+Exits 0 clean, 1 violation, 2 usage or setup error.
+EOF
+}
+
+die() { echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: $1" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+REPO_ROOT=""
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --repo-root=*)
+      REPO_ROOT="${1#--repo-root=}"
+      [ -n "$REPO_ROOT" ] || die "--repo-root= needs a directory"
+      shift ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) usage >&2; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [ -z "$REPO_ROOT" ]; then
+  case "$0" in
+    */*) SCRIPT_DIR="${0%/*}" ;;
+    *) SCRIPT_DIR="." ;;
+  esac
+  REPO_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."
+fi
+ROOT=$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) \
+  || die "not a git work tree: $REPO_ROOT"
+
+while IFS= read -r entry; do
+  [ -n "$entry" ] || continue
+  case "$entry" in
+    *'|'?*) ;;
+    *) die "ALLOWLIST entry has no reason: $entry" ;;
+  esac
+done <<EOF
+$ALLOWLIST
+EOF
+
+# allow_reason <path>: print the allowlist reason; return 1 when not listed.
+allow_reason() {
+  local want="$1" line
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    if [ "${line%%|*}" = "$want" ]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "${line#*|}"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done <<EOF
+$ALLOWLIST
+EOF
+  return 1
+}
+
+# :(glob) keeps * from crossing /, so only the ibl5/ root matches.
+specs=()
+for ext in $JSB_EXTS; do
+  specs+=(":(glob,icase)ibl5/*.$ext")
+done
+tracked=$(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- "${specs[@]}") \
+  || die "git ls-files failed in $ROOT"
+
+violations=0
+allowed=0
+while IFS= read -r path; do
+  [ -n "$path" ] || continue
+  if reason=$(allow_reason "$path"); then
+    allowed=$((allowed + 1))
+    echo "ok   $path (allowlisted: $reason)"
+  else
+    violations=$((violations + 1))
+    echo "FAIL $path is a git-tracked JSB runtime data file." >&2
+    echo "     The runtime may overwrite this path, and a deploy reset restores the stale committed content." >&2
+    echo "     Add it to ALLOWLIST in bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files with a reason, or move the fixture under ibl5/tests/." >&2
+  fi
+done <<EOF
+$tracked
+EOF
+
+if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
+  echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: $violations violation(s)" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: clean ($allowed allowlisted)"

+esac
+GATE="$(cd "$HERE" && pwd)/check-gitignore-negated-data-files"
+[ -x "$GATE" ] || { echo "FAIL setup: $GATE missing or not executable"; exit 1; }
+
+TMP=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
+failures=0
+
+# mkrepo <name> [path ...]: init $TMP/<name> and commit each path (content "x").

+  local repo="$TMP/$1" f
+  shift
+  mkdir -p "$repo/ibl5"
+  git -C "$repo" init -q
+  printf 'readme\n' > "$repo/ibl5/README"

+# expect <case> <exit> <substring> <command> [args ...]: run from cwd /.
+expect() {
+  local name="$1" want="$2" needle="$3" out rc
+  shift 3
+  rc=0

+    failures=$((failures + 1))

+
+mkrepo mixed ibl5/IBL5.sch ibl5/Foo.sch
+expect mixed_fails_on_unlisted 1 "FAIL ibl5/Foo.sch" "$GATE" --repo-root="$TMP/mixed"
+
+mkrepo nested ibl5/tests/fixtures/X.plr ibl5/sub/Y.sch
+expect nested_paths_ignored 0 "clean (0 allowlisted)" "$GATE" --repo-root="$TMP/nested"
+
+mkrepo upper ibl5/X.PLR

+expect space_form_rejected 2 "unknown argument: --repo-root" "$GATE" --repo-root "$TMP/clean"
+expect empty_repo_root_rejected 2 "needs a directory" "$GATE" --repo-root=

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+---
+description: ADR-0277. A CI gate, bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files, fails when a JSB runtime data file at the ibl5/ root is git-tracked without an allowlist reason, so a deploy reset cannot restore a stale committed copy over live data
+last_verified: 2026-11-21
+---
+
+# ADR-0277: Gate git-tracked JSB data files at the ibl5/ root
+
+**Status:** Accepted
+**Date:** 2026-11-21
+
+## Context
+
+The deploy job in `.github/workflows/main.yml` runs `git reset --hard origin/production` on the server. That command restores every tracked file to its committed copy. Ignored files survive it.
+
+The runtime and manual uploads replace JSB data files (`.plr`, `.sch`, `.lge`, and 11 other extensions) at the `ibl5/` root. When one of those files is tracked, the next deploy puts the stale committed copy back. A `.gitignore` negation (`!`) or a `git add -f` can track one without anyone noticing. The retrospective class registry first recorded this class on 2026-08-10, from PR #1834. Its only defense was a prose row in `.claude/review-shared/_plan-verification.md`, and that row only fires for work that goes through `/plan`.
+
+Three such files stay tracked on purpose. `ibl5/IBL5.lge` and `ibl5/IBL5.sch` are test fixtures. `ibl5/Olympics.sch` is the disk fallback that `ibl5/classes/Updater/JsbSourceResolver.php` reads when an uploaded archive has no `.sch` entry.
+
+## Decision
+
+`bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files` lists the git index with one `git ls-files` call. Its `:(glob,icase)` pathspecs cover the 14 JSB extensions at the `ibl5/` root. The gate fails on any listed path missing from the `ALLOWLIST` inside the script. Every allowlist entry must carry a reason, and the gate exits 2 on an entry without one. Files under `ibl5/tests/` are out of scope.
+
+CI runs the gate as a step in the `static-guards` job of `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, on every PR with no path filter. Its fixture harness `bin/test-check-gitignore-negated-data-files` runs in leg 0 of `.github/workflows/harness-legs.txt`.
+
+## Alternatives Considered
+
+- **Parse `.gitignore` for `!` negations.** Rejected because `git add -f` tracks a file with no negation line. The index is what a deploy reset restores.
+- **Loop over every tracked `ibl5/` path in bash.** Rejected because a per-file loop is slow under bash 3.2, and `bin/test-check-phpunit-hygiene` records a bash 3.2 heap crash from one.
+- **Run the gate from `.github/workflows/pr-meta-checks.yml`.** Rejected because that workflow's hygiene step sits behind a path filter. A forced add can land in any PR.
+- **Extend `bin/check-phpunit-hygiene`.** Rejected because that gate reads test-file contents, and an index scan is a separate job.
+- **Keep the prose row only.** Rejected because prose cannot stop a forced add made outside `/plan`.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- Positive: a newly tracked JSB data file at the `ibl5/` root fails CI before it can reach a deploy.
+- Positive: each tracked exception carries its reason next to the path, in the script.
+- Negative: the three allowlisted files still revert on deploy. A hand-uploaded newer `ibl5/Olympics.sch` would go back to the committed copy without a warning.
+- Negative: the gate does not fail on an allowlist entry whose file is no longer tracked.
+- Negative: one more `bin/check-*` gate and one more `bin/test-*` harness to maintain.
+
