@@ -0,0 +1,171 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# <!-- no-adr: additive lint gate over bin/ agent permission flags; ADR-0093 already owns the agent trust boundary this gate checks -->
+# bin/check-agent-allowlist — CI gate: a headless claude run under bin/ must not
+# get a wider grant than its comments document.
+#
+# Why: PR #3379 shipped bin/sim-recap-tick with an auto-approving permission
+# mode and an allow rule for the raw mysql client, which can run shell commands
+# through `system` and `\!`. Review caught it three times (backlog issue 1609).
+# This gate fails the PR that adds such a grant without a documented reason.
+#
+# Usage: bin/check-agent-allowlist   (scans the repo that holds this script)
+# gate-backtest-argv:
+# ---
+# A finding is accepted by a comment `# agent-allowlist-ok: <reason>` whose
+# reason is 15+ chars, on the flagged line itself or in the unbroken comment
+# block directly above the first line of the backslash-continued command.
+# ---
+# Fail closed: not a git repo, a git error, or no tracked bin/ files exits 2.
+PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin${PATH:+:$PATH}"; export PATH
+
+usage() {
+    cat <<'EOF'
+Usage: bin/check-agent-allowlist
+
+CI gate: scans tracked files under bin/ (skipping bin/test-* and *.md) for a
+headless claude run that gets
+  --permission-mode acceptEdits or bypassPermissions, or
+  an allow rule (--allowedTools / --tools) whose Bash(...) binary is a
+  shell-capable client (mysql, psql, bash, ssh, ...) or a $VARIABLE, or
+  a bare Bash, Bash(*) or Bash(*:*) rule written on the command line,
+and exits 1 unless a "# agent-allowlist-ok: <reason of 15+ chars>" comment
+sits on the line or in the unbroken comment block above the command.
+
+Exit codes:
+  0  No undocumented grant found
+  1  One or more findings (printed as path:line: kind: detail)
+  2  Usage error, not a git repo, or no tracked files under bin/
+EOF
+}
+
+die() { echo "check-agent-allowlist: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+set -eu
+
+case "${1:-}" in
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    "") ;;
+    *) usage >&2; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
+esac
+
+SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+if ! ROOT=$(git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null); then
+    die "not inside a git repo: $SCRIPT_DIR"
+fi
+if ! FILES=$(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- bin); then
+    die "git ls-files failed in $ROOT"
+fi
+[ -n "$FILES" ] || die "no tracked files under bin/ in $ROOT"
+
+AWK_PROG='
+function trim(s) { sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", s); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", s); return s }
+function marker_ok(s,   m) {
+    if (!match(s, /#[[:space:]]*agent-allowlist-ok:/)) return 0
+    m = trim(substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH))
+    return length(m) >= 15
+}
+function covered(n,   s, k) {
+    if (marker_ok(line[n])) return 1
+    s = n
+    while (s > 1 && line[s-1] ~ /\\[[:space:]]*$/) s--
+    for (k = s - 1; k >= 1 && line[k] ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/; k--)
+        if (marker_ok(line[k])) return 1
+    return 0
+}
+function report(n, kind, detail) {
+    if (!covered(n)) printf "%s:%d: %s: %s\n", path, n, kind, detail
+}
+function is_allow_flag(f) { return f ~ /^--(allowed-?[Tt]ools|tools)$/ }
+# last_flag: the last --flag word on s, or "" when s has none.
+function last_flag(s,   f) {
+    f = ""
+    while (match(s, /(^|[[:space:]])--[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*/)) {
+        f = substr(s, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", f)
+        s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
+    }
+    return f
+}
+# allow_text: the text of s that follows an allow flag, minus a trailing
+# comment. on=1 means s starts inside allow context (continued statement).
+function allow_text(s, on,   out, f) {
+    sub(/[[:space:]]#.*$/, "", s)
+    out = ""
+    while (match(s, /(^|[[:space:]])--[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*/)) {

+#!/bin/bash
+# bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files: fails when a JSB runtime data file at
+# the ibl5/ root is git-tracked (usually force-tracked by a .gitignore "!"
+# negation) and is not on the ALLOWLIST below.
+#
+# The deploy job in .github/workflows/main.yml runs
+# `git reset --hard origin/production`, which restores every tracked file. A
+# tracked data file that the runtime or a manual upload replaced on the server
+# goes back to the stale committed copy on the next deploy. Ignored files survive.
+#
+# Scope: the extensions in JSB_EXTS, ibl5/ root only, extension case-insensitive.
+# Fixtures under ibl5/tests/ are out of scope.
+# Exits 0 (clean), 1 (tracked data file not allowlisted), 2 (usage or setup error).
+#
+# CI (tests.yml) runs it with no arguments; the script finds the repo from its own path.
+# gate-backtest-argv:
+set -euo pipefail
+
+JSB_EXTS="lge sch plr sco car trn his asw rcb awa dra ret hof plb"
+
+# One entry per line: <repo-relative path>|<why it must stay tracked>.
+# Every entry needs a reason. Prefer moving a fixture under ibl5/tests/.
+ALLOWLIST='
+ibl5/IBL5.lge|fixture for LgeFileParserTest and LeagueConfigServiceTest
+ibl5/IBL5.sch|fixture for SchFileParserTest and e2e engine-shadow-spawn-on-update
+ibl5/Olympics.sch|JsbSourceResolver disk fallback when the archive has no .sch entry'
+
+usage() {
+  cat <<'EOF'
+Usage: bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files [--repo-root=<dir>] [--help|-h]
+Fails when a JSB runtime data file at the ibl5/ root is git-tracked and not
+allowlisted in this script. --repo-root=<dir> scans another git work tree
+(the = form is required). Default: the repo holding this script.
+Exits 0 clean, 1 violation, 2 usage or setup error.
+EOF
+}
+
+die() { echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: $1" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+REPO_ROOT=""
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --repo-root=*)
+      REPO_ROOT="${1#--repo-root=}"
+      [ -n "$REPO_ROOT" ] || die "--repo-root= needs a directory"
+      shift ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) usage >&2; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [ -z "$REPO_ROOT" ]; then
+  case "$0" in
+    */*) SCRIPT_DIR="${0%/*}" ;;
+    *) SCRIPT_DIR="." ;;
+  esac
+  REPO_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."
+fi
+ROOT=$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) \
+  || die "not a git work tree: $REPO_ROOT"
+
+while IFS= read -r entry; do
+  [ -n "$entry" ] || continue
+  case "$entry" in
+    *'|'?*) ;;
+    *) die "ALLOWLIST entry has no reason: $entry" ;;
+  esac
+done <<EOF
+$ALLOWLIST
+EOF
+
+# allow_reason <path>: print the allowlist reason; return 1 when not listed.
+allow_reason() {
+  local want="$1" line
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    if [ "${line%%|*}" = "$want" ]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "${line#*|}"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done <<EOF
+$ALLOWLIST
+EOF
+  return 1
+}
+
+# :(glob) keeps * from crossing /, so only the ibl5/ root matches.
+specs=()
+for ext in $JSB_EXTS; do
+  specs+=(":(glob,icase)ibl5/*.$ext")
+done
+tracked=$(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- "${specs[@]}") \
+  || die "git ls-files failed in $ROOT"
+
+violations=0
+allowed=0
+while IFS= read -r path; do
+  [ -n "$path" ] || continue
+  if reason=$(allow_reason "$path"); then
+    allowed=$((allowed + 1))
+    echo "ok   $path (allowlisted: $reason)"
+  else
+    violations=$((violations + 1))
+    echo "FAIL $path is a git-tracked JSB runtime data file." >&2
+    echo "     The runtime may overwrite this path, and a deploy reset restores the stale committed content." >&2
+    echo "     Add it to ALLOWLIST in bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files with a reason, or move the fixture under ibl5/tests/." >&2
+  fi
+done <<EOF
+$tracked
+EOF
+
+if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
+  echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: $violations violation(s)" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: clean ($allowed allowlisted)"

+expect allowlisted_passes 0 "clean (3 allowlisted)" "$GATE" --repo-root="$TMP/allow"
+
+mkrepo mixed ibl5/IBL5.sch ibl5/Foo.sch
+expect mixed_fails_on_unlisted 1 "FAIL ibl5/Foo.sch" "$GATE" --repo-root="$TMP/mixed"
+
+mkrepo nested ibl5/tests/fixtures/X.plr ibl5/sub/Y.sch
+expect nested_paths_ignored 0 "clean (0 allowlisted)" "$GATE" --repo-root="$TMP/nested"

+expect default_root_arbitrary_cwd 1 "FAIL ibl5/X.plr" "$TMP/plr/bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files"
+
+expect unknown_flag_rejected 2 "unknown argument: --bogus" "$GATE" --bogus
+expect space_form_rejected 2 "unknown argument: --repo-root" "$GATE" --repo-root "$TMP/clean"
+expect empty_repo_root_rejected 2 "needs a directory" "$GATE" --repo-root=
+mkdir -p "$TMP/plain"
+expect not_a_repo_rejected 2 "not a git work tree" "$GATE" --repo-root="$TMP/plain"

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+---
+description: ADR-0277. A CI gate, bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files, fails when a JSB runtime data file at the ibl5/ root is git-tracked without an allowlist reason, so a deploy reset cannot restore a stale committed copy over live data
+last_verified: 2026-11-21
+---
+
+# ADR-0277: Gate git-tracked JSB data files at the ibl5/ root
+
+**Status:** Accepted
+**Date:** 2026-11-21
+
+## Context
+
+The deploy job in `.github/workflows/main.yml` runs `git reset --hard origin/production` on the server. That command restores every tracked file to its committed copy. Ignored files survive it.
+
+The runtime and manual uploads replace JSB data files (`.plr`, `.sch`, `.lge`, and 11 other extensions) at the `ibl5/` root. When one of those files is tracked, the next deploy puts the stale committed copy back. A `.gitignore` negation (`!`) or a `git add -f` can track one without anyone noticing. The retrospective class registry first recorded this class on 2026-08-10, from PR #1834. Its only defense was a prose row in `.claude/review-shared/_plan-verification.md`, and that row only fires for work that goes through `/plan`.
+
+Three such files stay tracked on purpose. `ibl5/IBL5.lge` and `ibl5/IBL5.sch` are test fixtures. `ibl5/Olympics.sch` is the disk fallback that `ibl5/classes/Updater/JsbSourceResolver.php` reads when an uploaded archive has no `.sch` entry.
+
+## Decision
+
+`bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files` lists the git index with one `git ls-files` call. Its `:(glob,icase)` pathspecs cover the 14 JSB extensions at the `ibl5/` root. The gate fails on any listed path missing from the `ALLOWLIST` inside the script. Every allowlist entry must carry a reason, and the gate exits 2 on an entry without one. Files under `ibl5/tests/` are out of scope.
+
+CI runs the gate as a step in the `static-guards` job of `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, on every PR with no path filter. Its fixture harness `bin/test-check-gitignore-negated-data-files` runs in leg 0 of `.github/workflows/harness-legs.txt`.
+
+## Alternatives Considered
+
+- **Parse `.gitignore` for `!` negations.** Rejected because `git add -f` tracks a file with no negation line. The index is what a deploy reset restores.
+- **Loop over every tracked `ibl5/` path in bash.** Rejected because a per-file loop is slow under bash 3.2, and `bin/test-check-phpunit-hygiene` records a bash 3.2 heap crash from one.
+- **Run the gate from `.github/workflows/pr-meta-checks.yml`.** Rejected because that workflow's hygiene step sits behind a path filter. A forced add can land in any PR.
+- **Extend `bin/check-phpunit-hygiene`.** Rejected because that gate reads test-file contents, and an index scan is a separate job.
+- **Keep the prose row only.** Rejected because prose cannot stop a forced add made outside `/plan`.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- Positive: a newly tracked JSB data file at the `ibl5/` root fails CI before it can reach a deploy.
+- Positive: each tracked exception carries its reason next to the path, in the script.
+- Negative: the three allowlisted files still revert on deploy. A hand-uploaded newer `ibl5/Olympics.sch` would go back to the committed copy without a warning.
+- Negative: the gate does not fail on an allowlist entry whose file is no longer tracked.
+- Negative: one more `bin/check-*` gate and one more `bin/test-*` harness to maintain.
+
+## References
+
+- `bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files`
+- `bin/test-check-gitignore-negated-data-files`
+- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`
+- `.github/workflows/harness-legs.txt`
+- `.github/workflows/main.yml`
+- `ibl5/classes/Updater/JsbSourceResolver.php`
+- `ibl5/docs/retrospective-class-registry.md`
+- `.claude/review-shared/_plan-verification.md`

@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# Hold predicates in bin/lib/pr-armable.sh decide whether a PR may merge from
+# its changed-file list. `gh pr view/list --json files` gives `.path` objects
+# with no old path for a rename and stops at 100 files, so a PR that renames a
+# held path away (the engine golden snapshot, a UI file) skipped the hold
+# (backlog#1799, PR 3760 thread 4505747687). Only the REST list from
+# `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/N/files --paginate` carries `.previous_filename`.
+#
+# Rule A: the predicate bodies never read gh's `.path`.
+# Rule B: every predicate call passes a variable that a REST pulls/N/files call
+# assigns in the same file. Informational `--json files` users (overlap scans,
+# digests, notifications) call no predicate and are never flagged.
+#
+# Whole-tree, never diff-scoped: the live callers sat in files the fixing PR
+# did not touch. A call line may end `# files-json-ok: <reason>` (15+ chars).
+#
+# gate-backtest-argv:
+# gate-backtest-reads: bin/* .claude/review-shared/* .github/*
+#
+# Exit codes: 0 = pass, 1 = findings, 2 = usage error or missing anchor.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+MARKER_MIN_LEN=15
+LIB_REL="bin/lib/pr-armable.sh"
+# Hold predicate and the 1-based position of its file-list argument.
+HOLD_FNS="pr_golden_hold:1 pr_ui_hold:1 pr_docs_refresh_hold:2 pr_manual_testing_clearance:2"
+BODY_FNS="pr_golden_hold pr_ui_hold pr_docs_refresh_hold"
+
+usage() { echo "usage: bin/check-gh-pr-files-rename-old-path [--root DIR]" >&2; exit 2; }
+root="."
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+    case "$1" in
+        --root) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage; root="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+        *) usage ;;
+    esac
+done
+lib="$root/$LIB_REL"
+[ -f "$lib" ] || { echo "anchor missing: $LIB_REL under $root" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+hits=0
+marker_ok() { # <line>: 0 when it ends with a files-json-ok marker of MARKER_MIN_LEN+ chars
+    local reason
+    case "$1" in *'# files-json-ok:'*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
+    reason="$(printf '%s' "${1##*# files-json-ok:}" | sed -E 's/^[[:space:]]+//; s/[[:space:]]+$//')"
+    [ "${#reason}" -ge "$MARKER_MIN_LEN" ]
+}
+
+for fn in $BODY_FNS; do
+    if ! grep -qE "^${fn}\(\) \{" "$lib"; then
+        echo "anchor missing: ${fn}() in $LIB_REL" >&2; exit 2
+    fi
+    while IFS=: read -r ln text; do
+        marker_ok "$text" && continue
+        echo "$LIB_REL:$ln: $fn reads gh's .path; read the REST .filename and .previous_filename"
+        hits=$((hits + 1))
+    done < <(awk -v fn="$fn" '
+        $0 ~ ("^" fn "\\(\\) \\{") { inb = 1; next }
+        inb && /^\}/ { inb = 0 }
+        inb && $0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/ && $0 ~ /\.path([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)/ { print NR ":" $0 }' "$lib")
+done
+
+while IFS= read -r f; do
+    rel="${f#"$root"/}"
+    for spec in $HOLD_FNS; do
+        fn="${spec%%:*}"; pos="${spec##*:}"; skip=""; i=1
+        while [ "$i" -lt "$pos" ]; do skip="${skip}[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]+"; i=$((i + 1)); done
+        re='(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])'"$fn"'[[:space:]]+'"$skip"'"?\$\{?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)'
+        while IFS=: read -r ln text; do
+            [[ "$text" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
+            [[ "$text" =~ $re ]] || continue
+            var="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
+            marker_ok "$text" && continue
+            if grep -qE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])${var}=.*pulls/[^[:space:]]*/files" "$f"; then continue; fi
+            echo "$rel:$ln: $fn reads \$$var, which no REST pulls/N/files call assigns (gh --json files drops a rename's old path and caps at 100)"
+            hits=$((hits + 1))
+        done < <(grep -nE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])${fn}[[:space:]]" "$f" || true)
+    done
+done < <(find "$root/bin" "$root/.claude/review-shared" "$root/.github" -type f \
+    \( -name '*.sh' -o -name '*.yml' -o -name '*.yaml' -o ! -name '*.*' \) ! -name 'test-*' 2>/dev/null | sort)
+
+if [ "$hits" -gt 0 ]; then
+    echo "FAIL: $hits hold-predicate site(s) read a file list without a rename's old path" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+echo "ok: every hold predicate reads the REST pulls/N/files list"

+if [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then echo "ok: C10 usage"; else echo "FAIL: C10 usage — want rc 2, got $rc"; fail=1; fi
+
+# C11 real tree
+run_case "C11 real tree" 0 "$REPO_ROOT"
+

+#!/bin/bash
+# bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files: fails when a JSB runtime data file at
+# the ibl5/ root is git-tracked (usually force-tracked by a .gitignore "!"
+# negation) and is not on the ALLOWLIST below.
+#
+# The deploy job in .github/workflows/main.yml runs
+# `git reset --hard origin/production`, which restores every tracked file. A
+# tracked data file that the runtime or a manual upload replaced on the server
+# goes back to the stale committed copy on the next deploy. Ignored files survive.
+#
+# Scope: the extensions in JSB_EXTS, ibl5/ root only, extension case-insensitive.
+# Fixtures under ibl5/tests/ are out of scope.
+# Exits 0 (clean), 1 (tracked data file not allowlisted), 2 (usage or setup error).
+#
+# CI (tests.yml) runs it with no arguments; the script finds the repo from its own path.
+# gate-backtest-argv:
+set -euo pipefail
+
+JSB_EXTS="lge sch plr sco car trn his asw rcb awa dra ret hof plb"
+
+# One entry per line: <repo-relative path>|<why it must stay tracked>.
+# Every entry needs a reason. Prefer moving a fixture under ibl5/tests/.
+ALLOWLIST='
+ibl5/IBL5.lge|fixture for LgeFileParserTest and LeagueConfigServiceTest
+ibl5/IBL5.sch|fixture for SchFileParserTest and e2e engine-shadow-spawn-on-update
+ibl5/Olympics.sch|JsbSourceResolver disk fallback when the archive has no .sch entry'
+
+usage() {
+  cat <<'EOF'
+Usage: bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files [--repo-root=<dir>] [--help|-h]
+Fails when a JSB runtime data file at the ibl5/ root is git-tracked and not
+allowlisted in this script. --repo-root=<dir> scans another git work tree
+(the = form is required). Default: the repo holding this script.
+Exits 0 clean, 1 violation, 2 usage or setup error.
+EOF
+}
+
+die() { echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: $1" >&2; exit 2; }
+
+REPO_ROOT=""
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --repo-root=*)
+      REPO_ROOT="${1#--repo-root=}"
+      [ -n "$REPO_ROOT" ] || die "--repo-root= needs a directory"
+      shift ;;
+    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) usage >&2; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+if [ -z "$REPO_ROOT" ]; then
+  case "$0" in
+    */*) SCRIPT_DIR="${0%/*}" ;;
+    *) SCRIPT_DIR="." ;;
+  esac
+  REPO_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."
+fi
+ROOT=$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) \
+  || die "not a git work tree: $REPO_ROOT"
+
+while IFS= read -r entry; do
+  [ -n "$entry" ] || continue
+  case "$entry" in
+    *'|'?*) ;;
+    *) die "ALLOWLIST entry has no reason: $entry" ;;
+  esac
+done <<EOF
+$ALLOWLIST
+EOF
+
+# allow_reason <path>: print the allowlist reason; return 1 when not listed.
+allow_reason() {
+  local want="$1" line
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    if [ "${line%%|*}" = "$want" ]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "${line#*|}"
+      return 0
+    fi
+  done <<EOF
+$ALLOWLIST
+EOF
+  return 1
+}
+
+# :(glob) keeps * from crossing /, so only the ibl5/ root matches.
+specs=()
+for ext in $JSB_EXTS; do
+  specs+=(":(glob,icase)ibl5/*.$ext")
+done
+tracked=$(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- "${specs[@]}") \
+  || die "git ls-files failed in $ROOT"
+
+violations=0
+allowed=0
+while IFS= read -r path; do
+  [ -n "$path" ] || continue
+  if reason=$(allow_reason "$path"); then
+    allowed=$((allowed + 1))
+    echo "ok   $path (allowlisted: $reason)"
+  else
+    violations=$((violations + 1))
+    echo "FAIL $path is a git-tracked JSB runtime data file." >&2
+    echo "     The runtime may overwrite this path, and a deploy reset restores the stale committed content." >&2
+    echo "     Add it to ALLOWLIST in bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files with a reason, or move the fixture under ibl5/tests/." >&2
+  fi
+done <<EOF
+$tracked
+EOF
+
+if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
+  echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: $violations violation(s)" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+echo "check-gitignore-negated-data-files: clean ($allowed allowlisted)"

+
+mkrepo mixed ibl5/IBL5.sch ibl5/Foo.sch

+
+mkrepo nested ibl5/tests/fixtures/X.plr ibl5/sub/Y.sch

+mkrepo upper ibl5/X.PLR

+

+expect space_form_rejected 2 "unknown argument: --repo-root" "$GATE" --repo-root "$TMP/clean"
+expect empty_repo_root_rejected 2 "needs a directory" "$GATE" --repo-root=

@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+---
+description: ADR-0277. A CI gate, bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files, fails when a JSB runtime data file at the ibl5/ root is git-tracked without an allowlist reason, so a deploy reset cannot restore a stale committed copy over live data
+last_verified: 2026-11-21
+---
+
+# ADR-0277: Gate git-tracked JSB data files at the ibl5/ root
+
+**Status:** Accepted
+**Date:** 2026-11-21
+
+## Context
+
+The deploy job in `.github/workflows/main.yml` runs `git reset --hard origin/production` on the server. That command restores every tracked file to its committed copy. Ignored files survive it.
+
+The runtime and manual uploads replace JSB data files (`.plr`, `.sch`, `.lge`, and 11 other extensions) at the `ibl5/` root. When one of those files is tracked, the next deploy puts the stale committed copy back. A `.gitignore` negation (`!`) or a `git add -f` can track one without anyone noticing. The retrospective class registry first recorded this class on 2026-08-10, from PR #1834. Its only defense was a prose row in `.claude/review-shared/_plan-verification.md`, and that row only fires for work that goes through `/plan`.
+
+Three such files stay tracked on purpose. `ibl5/IBL5.lge` and `ibl5/IBL5.sch` are test fixtures. `ibl5/Olympics.sch` is the disk fallback that `ibl5/classes/Updater/JsbSourceResolver.php` reads when an uploaded archive has no `.sch` entry.
+
+## Decision
+
+`bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files` lists the git index with one `git ls-files` call. Its `:(glob,icase)` pathspecs cover the 14 JSB extensions at the `ibl5/` root. The gate fails on any listed path missing from the `ALLOWLIST` inside the script. Every allowlist entry must carry a reason, and the gate exits 2 on an entry without one. Files under `ibl5/tests/` are out of scope.
+
+CI runs the gate as a step in the `static-guards` job of `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, on every PR with no path filter. Its fixture harness `bin/test-check-gitignore-negated-data-files` runs in leg 0 of `.github/workflows/harness-legs.txt`.
+
+## Alternatives Considered
+
+- **Parse `.gitignore` for `!` negations.** Rejected because `git add -f` tracks a file with no negation line. The index is what a deploy reset restores.
+- **Loop over every tracked `ibl5/` path in bash.** Rejected because a per-file loop is slow under bash 3.2, and `bin/test-check-phpunit-hygiene` records a bash 3.2 heap crash from one.
+- **Run the gate from `.github/workflows/pr-meta-checks.yml`.** Rejected because that workflow's hygiene step sits behind a path filter. A forced add can land in any PR.
+- **Extend `bin/check-phpunit-hygiene`.** Rejected because that gate reads test-file contents, and an index scan is a separate job.
+- **Keep the prose row only.** Rejected because prose cannot stop a forced add made outside `/plan`.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- Positive: a newly tracked JSB data file at the `ibl5/` root fails CI before it can reach a deploy.
+- Positive: each tracked exception carries its reason next to the path, in the script.
+- Negative: the three allowlisted files still revert on deploy. A hand-uploaded newer `ibl5/Olympics.sch` would go back to the committed copy without a warning.
+- Negative: the gate does not fail on an allowlist entry whose file is no longer tracked.
+- Negative: one more `bin/check-*` gate and one more `bin/test-*` harness to maintain.
+
+## References
+
+- `bin/check-gitignore-negated-data-files`
+- `bin/test-check-gitignore-negated-data-files`
+- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`
+- `.github/workflows/harness-legs.txt`
+- `.github/workflows/main.yml`
+- `ibl5/classes/Updater/JsbSourceResolver.php`
+- `ibl5/docs/retrospective-class-registry.md`
+- `.claude/review-shared/_plan-verification.md`

+# ── Bug-bot auto-rebuild ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# The bot runs from the gitignored dist/bug-bot build in this checkout. When master
+# brings a new src/bug-bot commit, rebuild the dist and restart the bot, so nobody has
+# to do it by hand after a merge. bin/bug-pipeline-check reports the same staleness

+# Runs AFTER main: `kickstart -k` kills the bot at once, and the row work in main
+# calls the bot over HTTP. Never fails the tick. An idle tick costs one git log and
+# one find. A failed build writes no files (--noEmitOnError) and never restarts the
+# bot, so the old build keeps running.
+maybe_rebuild_bot() {
+    [ "$BOT_AUTO_REBUILD" = "1" ] || return 0

+    fi

+# shellcheck shell=bash
+# bug-bot-dist.sh: one staleness test for the bug-bot build, shared by
+# bin/bug-pipeline-check (reports it) and bin/bug-pipeline-tick (fixes it).
+# Sharing it means the check and the fixer cannot disagree on "stale".
+# Sourced, never executed. Sets no shell option and never calls exit.
+
+# bug_bot_mtime <file> — mtime epoch. GNU form first (shell-portability rule).
+bug_bot_mtime() {
+    stat -c %Y "$1" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m "$1" 2>/dev/null
+}
+
+# bug_bot_src_ct <repo-root> <git-bin> — commit time of the newest commit that
+# touched ibl5/IBLbot/src/bug-bot. Prints nothing when git has no answer.
+bug_bot_src_ct() {
+    "$2" -C "$1" log -1 --format=%ct -- ibl5/IBLbot/src/bug-bot 2>/dev/null
+}
+
+# bug_bot_dist_newest <repo-root> — newest file mtime under
+# the bug-bot folder in ibl5/IBLbot/dist/ (built, gitignored). Prints
+# nothing when the dist is absent or empty.
+bug_bot_dist_newest() {
+    local dist="$1/ibl5/IBLbot/dist/bug-bot" newest="" m f
+    [ -d "$dist" ] || return 0
+    while IFS= read -r f; do
+        m="$(bug_bot_mtime "$f")"
+        case "$m" in ''|*[!0-9]*) continue ;; esac
+        if [ -z "$newest" ] || [ "$m" -gt "$newest" ]; then newest="$m"; fi
+    done < <(find "$dist" -type f 2>/dev/null)
+    [ -n "$newest" ] && printf '%s\n' "$newest"
+    return 0
+}

+bpt_file_absent "$STUB/launchctl.log" "rebuild: fresh dist restarts nothing"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared rule: does a prior own "Code review" already cover the PR's current head?
+#
+# prior_review_covers_head PR [GH_CMD]
+#   exit 0  a review/comment by the current gh login covers headRefOid
+#   exit 1  not covered, or anything failed (fails toward running the review)
+#
+# A GitHub review covers the head when its commit.oid equals headRefOid. An
+# issue comment covers it only when its body carries the hidden reviewed-head
+# marker for that head (written by post_review_summary and harness/review.py).
+# Legacy unmarked comments never cover a head.
+#
+# Callers: bin/pr-review-now (embedded in the runner with `declare -f`) and
+# .claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md Step 1 (d) (sources this file).
+# This file is SOURCED, not executed.
+
+prior_review_covers_head() {
+    local pr="$1" gh="${2:-gh}" me n prog
+    me="$("$gh" api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
+    case "$me" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9-]*) return 1 ;; esac
+    prog='(.headRefOid // "") as $h
+      | if ($h | test("\\A[0-9a-f]{40}\\z")) then
+          [ (.comments[]?, .reviews[]?)
+            | select(.author.login == "'"$me"'")
+            | (.body // "") as $b
+            | select($b | test("\\A\\s*(#{1,6} +Code review|<details><summary>✅ Code review — no issues found</summary>)"))
+            | select((.commit.oid // "") == $h
+                     or ($b | contains("<!-- reviewed-head: " + $h + " -->"))) ]
+          | length
+        else 0 end'
+    n="$("$gh" pr view "$pr" --json comments,reviews,headRefOid --jq "$prog" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
+    case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+    [ "$n" -gt 0 ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared rule: does a prior own "Code review" already cover the PR's current head?
+#
+# prior_review_covers_head PR [GH_CMD]
+#   exit 0  a review/comment by the current gh login covers headRefOid
+#   exit 1  not covered, or anything failed (fails toward running the review)
+#
+# A GitHub review covers the head when its commit.oid equals headRefOid. An
+# issue comment covers it only when its body carries the hidden reviewed-head
+# marker for that head (written by post_review_summary and harness/review.py).
+# Legacy unmarked comments never cover a head.
+#
+# Callers: bin/pr-review-now (embedded in the runner with `declare -f`) and
+# .claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md Step 1 (d) (sources this file).
+# This file is SOURCED, not executed.
+
+prior_review_covers_head() {
+    local pr="$1" gh="${2:-gh}" me n prog
+    me="$("$gh" api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
+    case "$me" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9-]*) return 1 ;; esac
+    prog='(.headRefOid // "") as $h
+      | if ($h | test("\\A[0-9a-f]{40}\\z")) then
+          [ (.comments[]?, .reviews[]?)
+            | select(.author.login == "'"$me"'")
+            | (.body // "") as $b
+            | select($b | test("\\A\\s*(#{1,6} +Code review|<details><summary>✅ Code review — no issues found</summary>)"))
+            | select((.commit.oid // "") == $h
+                     or ($b | contains("<!-- reviewed-head: " + $h + " -->"))) ]
+          | length
+        else 0 end'
+    n="$("$gh" pr view "$pr" --json comments,reviews,headRefOid --jq "$prog" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
+    case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+    [ "$n" -gt 0 ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Shared rule: does a prior own "Code review" already cover the PR's current head?
+#
+# prior_review_covers_head PR [GH_CMD]
+#   exit 0  a review/comment by the current gh login covers headRefOid
+#   exit 1  not covered, or anything failed (fails toward running the review)
+#
+# A GitHub review covers the head when its commit.oid equals headRefOid. An
+# issue comment covers it only when its body carries the hidden reviewed-head
+# marker for that head (written by post_review_summary and harness/review.py).
+# Legacy unmarked comments never cover a head.
+#
+# Callers: bin/pr-review-now (embedded in the runner with `declare -f`) and
+# .claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md Step 1 (d) (sources this file).
+# This file is SOURCED, not executed.
+
+prior_review_covers_head() {
+    local pr="$1" gh="${2:-gh}" me n prog
+    me="$("$gh" api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
+    case "$me" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9-]*) return 1 ;; esac
+    prog='(.headRefOid // "") as $h
+      | if ($h | test("\\A[0-9a-f]{40}\\z")) then
+          [ (.comments[]?, .reviews[]?)
+            | select(.author.login == "'"$me"'")
+            | (.body // "") as $b
+            | select($b | test("\\A\\s*(#{1,6} +Code review|<details><summary>✅ Code review — no issues found</summary>)"))
+            | select((.commit.oid // "") == $h
+                     or ($b | contains("<!-- reviewed-head: " + $h + " -->"))) ]
+          | length
+        else 0 end'
+    n="$("$gh" pr view "$pr" --json comments,reviews,headRefOid --jq "$prog" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
+    case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
+    [ "$n" -gt 0 ]
+}

+"""Tests for the reviewed-head marker on clean Code review summaries (review.py)."""
+import os
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
+
+from harness.review import ReviewPhase, _reviewed_head_marker
+from harness.state import Classification, PlanInfo
+
+
+class _EmptyLlm:
+    """LLM stub: the code review agent finds nothing."""
+
+    def call(self, purpose, model, prompt, validate, max_retries=1, normalizer=None):
+        resp = []
+        if normalizer is not None:
+            resp = normalizer(resp)
+        validate(resp)
+        return resp
+
+    def call_tooled(self, purpose, model, prompt, *, cwd, allowed_tools=(), **kw):
+        return []
+
+
+class _NullGh:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.summary_calls = []
+
+    def post_review_findings(self, pr, sha, title, findings):
+        pass
+

+

 description: Faithful JSB 5.60 putback (OReb-continuation, OriginOffReb) shot resolution shipped UNCONDITIONALLY ON as the default live engine. The net-coupled un-boosted putback make-value is the suspected carrier of the empty-FGA shots-per-possession anti-coupling (ADR-0049 Cov(ln(FGA/POSS),lnPPS) ≈ −0.00087, real ≈ 0): low-efficiency teams miss putbacks more → more miss→ORB→retry loops → extra empty FGA → wrong-signed factor. Golden bytes change BY DESIGN (regenerated with -update); TestDeterminism stays green. Measured as a 2-config A/B (OFF=UnfaithfulPutback / ON=faithful) over the full backup archive (705 zips, stride 1, runs 20). Magnitude caveat: the factor gap closes ~8% and the headline does not flip (−0.001210 → −0.001120, real +0.000269) — the faithful form is A carrier, not THE dominant one, refining ADR-0053's null (make-value VARIANCE is not the carrier; the make-value FORM is, but the bulk stays structural to the empty-FGA volume loop, left to the OOS count axis ADR-0054 / offVolumeScale #974). Ships as faithful production behavior on RE-verified merits independent of magnitude. CORRECTION 2026-07-22 — divergence (2) is REVERSED: the 3pt-suppression claim rests on a decompile MISREAD. local_15c is the OReb *continuation* flag (the possession do-while's loop condition at 94379), assigned from the rebound routine at 94019, so the goto at 94024 is the loop-back for the next iteration, NOT a 3pt→2pt re-roll. 5.60 in fact CLEARS the shot-clock restriction on an OReb continuation (93278-93280), guaranteeing the full four-bucket set, and FUN_004e1ba0's reject-retry (97194-97196) has no OReb branch at all — putback 3pt IS reachable in 5.60. CORRECTION 2, 2026-07-23 — that reversal is WITHDRAWN and divergence (2) is REINSTATED on a corrected citation. +++ b/bin/lib/plan-matrix-rows.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+# shellcheck shell=bash
+# Shared Verification Matrix row parser. Sourced by bin/check-plan and
+# bin/lib/prefire-verify. A matrix row is `| N | what | type | timing | location |`.
+# A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`; it is swapped for a sentinel before the
+# split and restored afterward, so the restored cell is the runnable command.
+
+MSEN=$'\001'
+
+mtrim() { _s="${1#"${1%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; printf '%s' "${_s%"${_s##*[![:space:]]}"}"; }
+
+# matrix_split <row> — sets MC_NUM / MC_TYPE / MC_TIME / MC_LOC (trimmed, any
+# surrounding backticks stripped, pipes restored) and MC_PIPES (count of
+# STRUCTURAL pipes, i.e. after escaped pipes are hidden). Returns 1 for a
+# separator row or a row with no location cell.
+matrix_split() {
+    case "$1" in
+        *[!\ \|:-]*) : ;;
+        *) return 1 ;;              # separator / all-dashes row
+    esac
+    _r="${1//\\|/$MSEN}"
+    IFS='|' read -r _lead MC_NUM MC_WHAT MC_TYPE MC_TIME MC_LOC _rest <<< "$_r"
+    # shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by bin/check-plan gates
+    MC_PIPES=$(printf '%s' "$_r" | tr -cd '|' | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
+    MC_NUM=$(mtrim "$MC_NUM"); MC_TYPE=$(mtrim "$MC_TYPE"); MC_TIME=$(mtrim "$MC_TIME")
+    MC_WHAT=$(mtrim "$MC_WHAT")
+    MC_LOC=$(mtrim "${MC_LOC//$MSEN/|}")
+    case "$MC_LOC" in '`'*'`') MC_LOC=$(mtrim "${MC_LOC#\`}"); MC_LOC=$(mtrim "${MC_LOC%\`}") ;; esac
+    [ -n "$MC_LOC" ] || return 1
+    return 0
+}
+
+# plan_matrix_rows <plan-file> — prints "<num><TAB><command>" for each runnable
+# row of the plan's `## Verification Matrix` section. Runnable means: a real
+# data row, whole-cell CLI-executable type, post-impl timing, not a one-time
+# check, and not a post-merge location. Returns 2 when the plan has no
+# Verification Matrix heading, 0 otherwise (zero runnable rows is valid).
+plan_matrix_rows() {
+    local plan="$1" in_matrix=0 found=0 line type_lc
+    [ -f "$plan" ] || return 2
+    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
+        case "$line" in
+            '## Verification Matrix'*) in_matrix=1; found=1; continue ;;
+            '## '*) in_matrix=0; continue ;;
+        esac
+        [ "$in_matrix" -eq 1 ] || continue
+        case "$line" in '|'*) : ;; *) continue ;; esac
+        matrix_split "$line" || continue
+        case "$MC_NUM" in ''|'#') continue ;; esac
+        type_lc=$(printf '%s' "$MC_TYPE" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
+        # whole-cell match, optional parenthesized annotation
+        [[ "$type_lc" =~ ^cli[-\ ]executable(\ *\([^\)]*\))?$ ]] || continue
+        case "$MC_TIME" in *post-impl*) : ;; *) continue ;; esac
+        case "$MC_WHAT" in *'(one-time-check:'*) continue ;; esac
+        case "$MC_LOC" in *'post-merge:'*) continue ;; esac
+        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$MC_NUM" "$MC_LOC"
+    done < "$plan"
+    [ "$found" -eq 1 ] || return 2
+    return 0
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# bin/lib/prefire-verify — pre-fire verification gate.
+#
+# Re-runs three checks on the current working tree before /post-plan fires:
+#   1. every post-impl CLI-executable row of the plan's Verification Matrix
+#   2. the full default PHPUnit suite
+#   3. Infection on the changed classes at CI's thresholds (bin/mutation-diff)
+# It trusts no implementer-written ledger. Only this script writes pass records,
+# keyed by tree hash, in the per-worktree git dir. It fails closed.
+#
+# Usage: bin/lib/prefire-verify [--plan <path>] [--stage matrix|phpunit|infection|all]
+#                               [--base <ref>] [--bypass <reason>]
+# Exit codes:
+#   0  every requested stage passed (fresh run, or a valid pass record for this tree)
+#   1  a check failed (the message names the matrix row or the stage)
+#   2  usage error
+#   3  prerequisite missing: vendor/bin/phpunit, docker, the DB container, pcov
+#   4  the checks changed the working tree, so no pass record was written
+#
+# Test seams (used only by bin/test-prefire-verify):
+#   PREFIRE_PHPUNIT_CMD    default vendor/bin/phpunit, run from ibl5/
+#   PREFIRE_MUTATION_CMD   default bin/mutation-diff, run from the repo root
+#   PREFIRE_DB_PROBE_CMD   default bin/db-query "SELECT 1", run from the repo root
+#   PREFIRE_EXCLUDES_CMD   default bin/check-infection-excludes, run from ibl5/
+
+set -uo pipefail
+
+SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+# shellcheck source=bin/lib/plan-matrix-rows.sh
+source "$SELF_DIR/plan-matrix-rows.sh"
+# shellcheck source=bin/lib/branch-base.sh
+source "$SELF_DIR/branch-base.sh"
+
+say() { printf 'prefire-verify: %s\n' "$*"; }
+die() { local rc="$1"; shift; printf 'prefire-verify: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "$rc"; }
+
+PLAN=""
+STAGE="all"
+BASE_OPT=""
+BYPASS_REASON=""
+BYPASS_SET=0
+
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+    case "$1" in
+        --plan)   [ $# -ge 2 ] || die 2 "--plan needs a path"; PLAN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+        --stage)  [ $# -ge 2 ] || die 2 "--stage needs a value"; STAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+        --base)   [ $# -ge 2 ] || die 2 "--base needs a ref"; BASE_OPT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+        --bypass) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die 2 "--bypass needs a reason"; BYPASS_REASON="$2"; BYPASS_SET=1; shift 2 ;;
+        -h|--help) sed -n '2,22p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+        *) die 2 "unknown argument '$1'" ;;
+    esac
+done
+
+case "$STAGE" in
+    matrix|phpunit|infection|all) : ;;
+    *) die 2 "--stage must be matrix, phpunit, infection, or all (got '$STAGE')" ;;
+esac
+if [ "$BYPASS_SET" -eq 1 ] && [ -z "$BYPASS_REASON" ]; then
+    die 2 "--bypass needs a non-empty reason"
+fi
+if [ -n "$PLAN" ] && [ ! -f "$PLAN" ]; then
+    die 2 "plan file not found: $PLAN"
+fi
+# The check above reads --plan from the caller's cwd. The cd below moves to the
+# repo root, so pin the path now or a relative plan stops resolving.
+if [ -n "$PLAN" ]; then
+    PLAN="$(cd "$(dirname "$PLAN")" && pwd)/$(basename "$PLAN")"
+fi
+
+ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die 2 "not inside a git work tree"
+cd "$ROOT" || die 2 "cannot cd to $ROOT"

+prefire_tree_hash() {
+    local idx rc
+    idx=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/prefire-idx.XXXXXX") || return 1
+    cp "$(git rev-parse --git-path index)" "$idx" 2>/dev/null || true

+    rm -f "$idx"

+    fi

+    else

+    fi

+    [ -f "$f" ] || return 1

+    git status --short | head -n 20 >&2
+    exit 4
+fi
+say "all requested stages passed ($STAGES)"
+exit 0

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Tests bin/lib/prefire-verify (the pre-fire verification gate) and its wiring
+# into bin/post-plan-now, with stubbed PHPUnit / Infection / DB probe.
+#
+# Usage: bin/test-prefire-verify [case_name ...]
+# With no arguments every case runs; with arguments only the named cases run.
+# Prints `PASS <name>` / `FAIL <name>: <why>` per case. Exit 0 iff all pass.

+
+# shellcheck source=bin/lib/harness.sh

+

+printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n' > "$TMP/shims/security"
+printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$TMP/shims/launchctl"

+export PATH="$TMP/shims:$PATH"
+export IBL5_USAGE_GATE_STATE_DIR="$TMP/gate"
+mkdir -p "$IBL5_USAGE_GATE_STATE_DIR"
+export POSTPLAN_LOG_DIR="$TMP/runlog" PLAN_NOW_LOG_DIR="$TMP/runlog"
+unset CLAUDE_HEADLESS
+
+WHY=""      # failure reasons for the current case
+OUT=""      # combined stdout+stderr of the last run
+RC=0        # exit code of the last run
+
+note() { WHY="${WHY:+$WHY; }$*"; }
+want_rc() { [ "$RC" -eq "$1" ] || note "expected exit $1, got $RC"; }
+want_out() { grep -qF -- "$1" <<< "$OUT" || note "output lacks '$1'"; }
+refute_out() { if grep -qF -- "$1" <<< "$OUT"; then note "output unexpectedly has '$1'"; fi; }
+want_cnt() { # <counter> <n>
+    local got; got=$(cnt "$1")
+    [ "$got" -eq "$2" ] || note "counter $1 expected $2, got $got"
+}
+cnt() {
+    if [ -f "$CNT/$1" ]; then wc -l < "$CNT/$1" | tr -d ' '; else echo 0; fi
+}
+

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+    PLAN="$D/plan.md"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo run >> "$CNT/phpunit"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo run >> "$CNT/mutation"

+    3672)

+        echo "491 mutants were escaped"

+    prereq) echo "Error: pcov is not loaded"; exit 3 ;;
+    *) echo "Mutation Score Indicator (MSI): 100%"; exit 0 ;;

+# ADR-0227: Pre-fire verification gate in post-plan-now
+
+**Status:** Accepted
+**Date:** 2026-11-03
+**Deciders:** ajaynicolas
+
+## Context
+
+PR #3672 shipped with 491 of 2295 mutants escaped and CI's per-PR Infection job red. Its implementation ran no Infection before firing. Two paths fire a ship: a human or interactive session calling `bin/post-plan-now`, and the automouse runner calling `post-plan-now --foreground` from the handoff file. Neither checked that verification had run.
+
+## Decision
+
+- One gate script, `bin/lib/prefire-verify`, is called from `bin/post-plan-now` before any launch. It exits 9 on refusal.
+- Automouse's `bin/automouse/prompt-impl` Step 6.9 runs the same script stage by stage, so the impl agent can fix failures while it still has the tree.
+- The gate re-runs every check and trusts no implementer-written ledger. Pass records are keyed by tree hash and written only by the gate.
+- Infection runs through `bin/mutation-diff`, so CI's flags and MSI 100 live in one place (the per-PR check of ADR-0145).
+- The gate fails closed: a missing prerequisite, a timed-out stage, or a missing record all mean no fire.
+- The bypass, `--skip-verify=<reason>`, is human-only, needs a reason of at least 15 characters, is refused under `CLAUDE_HEADLESS`, and is logged to `prefire-verify-bypass.log` in the main checkout's `.git`.
+
+## Extend-before-add
+
+No existing host owns this. `bin/lib/plan-matrix-assertions` checks that a diff footprint exists and never executes a row. `bin/post-plan-now` is the host, but the same logic must also be callable stage by stage from the impl prompt, so it lives in `bin/lib/` and is called from both places. The matrix parser moved from `bin/check-plan` into the shared `bin/lib/plan-matrix-rows.sh`, so there is one parser.
+
+## Alternatives Considered
+
+- **Trust a ledger the implementer writes.** Rejected because: the check would then rest on the claim it exists to verify.
+- **Gate only in CI.** Rejected because: CI already has the Infection job and `#3672` shipped red anyway; the failure must reach the implementer before the fire.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- Negative: the first fire on a new tree costs a full PHPUnit run plus a changed-file mutation run.
+- Positive: a stage the impl session could not finish within its 600 s cap reruns at the fire point, inside the runner's remaining budget.
+- Neutral: ad-hoc runs with no plan keep PHPUnit and Infection and skip the matrix stage.
+- Neutral: fleet rescues (`--pr`) are gated too, and `--rebase-only` is exempt because it pushes no new content.
+
+## References
+
+- `bin/lib/prefire-verify`: the gate and its pass records.
+- `bin/test-prefire-verify`: the harness.
+- `bin/post-plan-now`: the fire point and exit 9.
+- `bin/automouse/prompt-impl`: Step 6.9.
+- `bin/mutation-diff`: the shared Infection runner.
+- `bin/lib/plan-matrix-rows.sh`: the shared matrix parser.
+- `.github/workflows/mutation-pr.yml`: the CI side of the same check.
+- `ibl5/docs/decisions/0145-mutation-pr-required-own-workflow.md`: the per-PR mutation check.

@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+# shellcheck shell=bash
+# Shared Verification Matrix row parser. Sourced by bin/check-plan and
+# bin/lib/prefire-verify. A matrix row is `| N | what | type | timing | location |`.
+# A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`; it is swapped for a sentinel before the
+# split and restored afterward, so the restored cell is the runnable command.
+
+MSEN=$'\001'
+
+mtrim() { _s="${1#"${1%%[![:space:]]*}"}"; printf '%s' "${_s%"${_s##*[![:space:]]}"}"; }
+
+# matrix_split <row> — sets MC_NUM / MC_TYPE / MC_TIME / MC_LOC (trimmed, any
+# surrounding backticks stripped, pipes restored) and MC_PIPES (count of
+# STRUCTURAL pipes, i.e. after escaped pipes are hidden). Returns 1 for a
+# separator row or a row with no location cell.
+matrix_split() {
+    case "$1" in
+        *[!\ \|:-]*) : ;;
+        *) return 1 ;;              # separator / all-dashes row
+    esac
+    _r="${1//\\|/$MSEN}"
+    IFS='|' read -r _lead MC_NUM MC_WHAT MC_TYPE MC_TIME MC_LOC _rest <<< "$_r"
+    # shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by bin/check-plan gates
+    MC_PIPES=$(printf '%s' "$_r" | tr -cd '|' | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
+    MC_NUM=$(mtrim "$MC_NUM"); MC_TYPE=$(mtrim "$MC_TYPE"); MC_TIME=$(mtrim "$MC_TIME")
+    MC_WHAT=$(mtrim "$MC_WHAT")
+    MC_LOC=$(mtrim "${MC_LOC//$MSEN/|}")
+    case "$MC_LOC" in '`'*'`') MC_LOC=$(mtrim "${MC_LOC#\`}"); MC_LOC=$(mtrim "${MC_LOC%\`}") ;; esac
+    [ -n "$MC_LOC" ] || return 1
+    return 0
+}
+
+# plan_matrix_rows <plan-file> — prints "<num><TAB><command>" for each runnable
+# row of the plan's `## Verification Matrix` section. Runnable means: a real
+# data row, whole-cell CLI-executable type, post-impl timing, not a one-time
+# check, and not a post-merge location. Returns 2 when the plan has no
+# Verification Matrix heading, 0 otherwise (zero runnable rows is valid).
+plan_matrix_rows() {
+    local plan="$1" in_matrix=0 found=0 line type_lc
+    [ -f "$plan" ] || return 2
+    while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do
+        case "$line" in
+            '## Verification Matrix'*) in_matrix=1; found=1; continue ;;
+            '## '*) in_matrix=0; continue ;;
+        esac
+        [ "$in_matrix" -eq 1 ] || continue
+        case "$line" in '|'*) : ;; *) continue ;; esac
+        matrix_split "$line" || continue
+        case "$MC_NUM" in ''|'#') continue ;; esac
+        type_lc=$(printf '%s' "$MC_TYPE" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
+        # whole-cell match, optional parenthesized annotation
+        [[ "$type_lc" =~ ^cli[-\ ]executable(\ *\([^\)]*\))?$ ]] || continue
+        case "$MC_TIME" in *post-impl*) : ;; *) continue ;; esac
+        case "$MC_WHAT" in *'(one-time-check:'*) continue ;; esac
+        case "$MC_LOC" in *'post-merge:'*) continue ;; esac
+        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$MC_NUM" "$MC_LOC"
+    done < "$plan"
+    [ "$found" -eq 1 ] || return 2
+    return 0
+}

index 0000000000..7a68de8ac7

+++ b/bin/lib/prefire-verify
@@ -0,0 +1,268 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# bin/lib/prefire-verify — pre-fire verification gate.
+#
+# Re-runs three checks on the current working tree before /post-plan fires:
+#   1. every post-impl CLI-executable row of the plan's Verification Matrix
+#   2. the full default PHPUnit suite
+#   3. Infection on the changed classes at CI's thresholds (bin/mutation-diff)
+# It trusts no implementer-written ledger. Only this script writes pass records,
+# keyed by tree hash, in the per-worktree git dir. It fails closed.
+#
+# Usage: bin/lib/prefire-verify [--plan <path>] [--stage matrix|phpunit|infection|all]
+#                               [--base <ref>] [--bypass <reason>]
+# Exit codes:
+#   0  every requested stage passed (fresh run, or a valid pass record for this tree)
+#   1  a check failed (the message names the matrix row or the stage)
+#   2  usage error
+#   3  prerequisite missing: vendor/bin/phpunit, docker, the DB container, pcov
+#   4  the checks changed the working tree, so no pass record was written
+#
+# Test seams (used only by bin/test-prefire-verify):
+#   PREFIRE_PHPUNIT_CMD    default vendor/bin/phpunit, run from ibl5/
+#   PREFIRE_MUTATION_CMD   default bin/mutation-diff, run from the repo root
+#   PREFIRE_DB_PROBE_CMD   default bin/db-query "SELECT 1", run from the repo root
+#   PREFIRE_EXCLUDES_CMD   default bin/check-infection-excludes, run from ibl5/
+
+set -uo pipefail
+
+SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+# shellcheck source=bin/lib/plan-matrix-rows.sh
+source "$SELF_DIR/plan-matrix-rows.sh"
+# shellcheck source=bin/lib/branch-base.sh
+source "$SELF_DIR/branch-base.sh"
+
+say() { printf 'prefire-verify: %s\n' "$*"; }
+die() { local rc="$1"; shift; printf 'prefire-verify: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "$rc"; }
+
+PLAN=""
+STAGE="all"
+BASE_OPT=""
+BYPASS_REASON=""
+BYPASS_SET=0
+
+while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
+    case "$1" in
+        --plan)   [ $# -ge 2 ] || die 2 "--plan needs a path"; PLAN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+        --stage)  [ $# -ge 2 ] || die 2 "--stage needs a value"; STAGE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+        --base)   [ $# -ge 2 ] || die 2 "--base needs a ref"; BASE_OPT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
+        --bypass) [ $# -ge 2 ] || die 2 "--bypass needs a reason"; BYPASS_REASON="$2"; BYPASS_SET=1; shift 2 ;;
+        -h|--help) sed -n '2,22p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
+        *) die 2 "unknown argument '$1'" ;;
+    esac
+done
+
+case "$STAGE" in
+    matrix|phpunit|infection|all) : ;;
+    *) die 2 "--stage must be matrix, phpunit, infection, or all (got '$STAGE')" ;;
+esac
+if [ "$BYPASS_SET" -eq 1 ] && [ -z "$BYPASS_REASON" ]; then
+    die 2 "--bypass needs a non-empty reason"
+fi
+if [ -n "$PLAN" ] && [ ! -f "$PLAN" ]; then
+    die 2 "plan file not found: $PLAN"
+fi
+
+ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die 2 "not inside a git work tree"
+cd "$ROOT" || die 2 "cannot cd to $ROOT"
+
+prefire_tree_hash() {
+    local idx rc
+    idx=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/prefire-idx.XXXXXX") || return 1
+    cp "$(git rev-parse --git-path index)" "$idx" 2>/dev/null || true
+    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" git add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+        && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" git write-tree
+    rc=$?
+    rm -f "$idx"
+    return $rc
+}
+
+TREE=$(prefire_tree_hash) || die 3 "cannot compute the working-tree hash"
+TREE7="${TREE:0:7}"
+STATE_DIR="$(git rev-parse --git-path prefire-verify)"
+mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" || die 3 "cannot create $STATE_DIR"
+
+# --- escape hatch (human only, logged) -------------------------------------
+if [ "$BYPASS_SET" -eq 1 ]; then
+    if [ "${CLAUDE_HEADLESS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
+        die 2 "--bypass is for a human at a terminal; refused under CLAUDE_HEADLESS"
+    fi
+    if [ "${#BYPASS_REASON}" -lt 15 ]; then
+        die 2 "--bypass needs a reason of at least 15 characters"
+    fi
+    BYPASS_LOG="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/prefire-verify-bypass.log"
+    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
+        "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
+        "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" "$TREE7" "${USER:-unknown}" "$BYPASS_REASON" \
+        >> "$BYPASS_LOG"
+    printf 'prefire-verify: BYPASSED (logged to %s): %s\n' "$BYPASS_LOG" "$BYPASS_REASON" >&2
+    exit 0
+fi
+
+# --- pass records -----------------------------------------------------------
+record_path() { # <stage> <key>
+    if [ -n "$2" ]; then
+        printf '%s/%s.%s.%s.pass' "$STATE_DIR" "$TREE" "$1" "$2"
+    else
+        printf '%s/%s.%s.pass' "$STATE_DIR" "$TREE" "$1"
+    fi
+}
+
+cache_hit() { # <stage> <key>; prints the cache message on a hit
+    local f body at
+    f=$(record_path "$1" "$2")
+    [ -f "$f" ] || return 1
+    body=$(cat "$f")
+    case " $body " in *" tree=$TREE "*) : ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
+    if [ -n "$2" ]; then
+        case " $body " in *" key=$2 "*) : ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
+    fi
+    at="${body#*at=}"; at="${at%% *}"
+    say "$1 pass cached for tree $TREE7 (recorded $at)"
+    return 0
+}
+
+write_record() { # <stage> <key>
+    printf 'stage=%s tree=%s key=%s at=%s by=prefire-verify\n' \
+        "$1" "$TREE" "${2:-none}" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" > "$(record_path "$1" "$2")"
+}
+
+# --- matrix stage -----------------------------------------------------------
+stage_matrix() {
+    local plan_sha rows rc num cmd log rows_rc
+    if [ -z "$PLAN" ]; then
+        say "SKIP matrix: no plan (ad-hoc path); PHPUnit and Infection still run"
+        return 0
+    fi
+    plan_sha=$(git hash-object "$PLAN")
+    cache_hit matrix "$plan_sha" && return 0
+
+    rows=$(plan_matrix_rows "$PLAN"); rows_rc=$?
+    if [ "$rows_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
+        say "FAIL plan has no Verification Matrix; no evidence to check" >&2
+        return 1
+    fi
+
+    # DB probe, once, before the first DB-touching row.
+    local db_re='db-query|docker|--group[= ]database|DatabaseIntegration|db-test-up|run-migrations|mariadb'
+    local first_db_num="" first_db_cmd=""
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r num cmd; do
+        [ -n "$num" ] || continue
+        if grep -Eq -- "$db_re" <<< "$cmd"; then first_db_num="$num"; first_db_cmd="$cmd"; break; fi
+    done <<< "$rows"
+    if [ -n "$first_db_num" ]; then
+        if [ -n "${PREFIRE_DB_PROBE_CMD:-}" ]; then
+            bash -c "$PREFIRE_DB_PROBE_CMD" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+        else
+            bin/db-query "SELECT 1" >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+        fi
+        if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
+            say "FAIL DB unreachable; matrix row $first_db_num needs it ($first_db_cmd). Start the worktree stack, then re-run" >&2
+            return 3
+        fi
+    fi
+
+    log="$STATE_DIR/$TREE.matrix.log"
+    : > "$log"
+    while IFS=$'\t' read -r num cmd; do
+        [ -n "$num" ] || continue
+        say "matrix row $num: $cmd"
+        printf '### row %s: %s\n' "$num" "$cmd" >> "$log"
+        bash -c "$cmd" </dev/null >> "$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
+        if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
+            say "FAIL matrix row $num exited $rc: $cmd" >&2
+            tail -n 30 "$log" >&2
+            return 1
+        fi
+    done <<< "$rows"
+    write_record matrix "$plan_sha"
+    say "matrix passed"
+    return 0
+}
+
+# --- phpunit stage ----------------------------------------------------------
+stage_phpunit() {
+    local log rc cmd="${PREFIRE_PHPUNIT_CMD:-vendor/bin/phpunit}"
+    cache_hit phpunit "" && return 0
+    if [ -z "${PREFIRE_PHPUNIT_CMD:-}" ] && [ ! -x ibl5/vendor/bin/phpunit ]; then
+        say "FAIL phpunit prerequisite missing: ibl5/vendor/bin/phpunit; run composer install in ibl5/" >&2
+        return 3
+    fi
+    log="$STATE_DIR/$TREE.phpunit.log"
+    (cd ibl5 && bash -c "$cmd") > "$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
+    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
+        say "FAIL phpunit: full default suite red (exit $rc); log: $log" >&2
+        tail -n 40 "$log" >&2
+        return 1
+    fi
+    write_record phpunit ""
+    say "phpunit passed"
+    return 0
+}
+
+# --- infection stage --------------------------------------------------------
+resolve_base() {
+    if [ -n "$BASE_OPT" ]; then
+        BASE_REF="$BASE_OPT"
+    elif _b=$(branch_base_resolve "$ROOT" "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)") && [ -n "$_b" ]; then
+        BASE_REF="$_b"   # branch_base_resolve already prints "origin/<name>"
+    else
+        BASE_REF="origin/master"
+    fi
+    BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$BASE_REF^{commit}") || {
+        say "FAIL base ref $BASE_REF does not resolve; run git fetch origin" >&2
+        return 3
+    }
+    return 0
+}
+
+stage_infection() {
+    local log rc cmd="${PREFIRE_MUTATION_CMD:-bin/mutation-diff}"
+    resolve_base || return 3
+    cache_hit infection "$BASE_SHA" && return 0
+    log="$STATE_DIR/$TREE.infection.log"
+
+    (cd ibl5 && bash -c "${PREFIRE_EXCLUDES_CMD:-bin/check-infection-excludes}") > "$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
+    if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
+        say "FAIL infection: check-infection-excludes red (exit $rc)" >&2
+        tail -n 20 "$log" >&2
+        return 1
+    fi
+
+    bash -c "$cmd \"\$1\"" _ "$BASE_REF" > "$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
+    case "$rc" in
+        0)
+            write_record infection "$BASE_SHA"
+            say "infection passed (or skipped: no changed classes) vs $BASE_REF"
+            return 0 ;;
+        2) say "FAIL infection: base ref unusable" >&2; rc=3 ;;
+        3) say "FAIL infection: prerequisite missing (pcov, docker, ibl5-mariadb, or db-test-up)" >&2
+           grep -E 'Error:' "$log" | tail -n 2 >&2; rc=3 ;;
+        4) say "FAIL infection: another bin/mutation-diff run holds /tmp/ibl5-mutation-diff.lock; re-run after it finishes" >&2; rc=3 ;;
+        5) say "FAIL infection: Infection matched no source files although classes changed" >&2; rc=1 ;;
+        *) say "FAIL infection: below CI threshold (min-msi=100) or coverage run red (exit $rc)" >&2; rc=1 ;;
+    esac
+    grep -E 'mutations were generated|escaped|Mutation Score Indicator|minimum required MSI' "$log" | tail -n 6 >&2
+    return "$rc"
+}
+
+# --- run --------------------------------------------------------------------
+case "$STAGE" in
+    all) STAGES="matrix phpunit infection" ;;
+    *)   STAGES="$STAGE" ;;
+esac
+
+for s in $STAGES; do
+    "stage_$s"; rc=$?
+    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || exit "$rc"
+done
+
+NEW_TREE=$(prefire_tree_hash) || die 3 "cannot recompute the working-tree hash"
+if [ "$NEW_TREE" != "$TREE" ]; then
+    # Drop every record this run wrote for the old tree.
+    rm -f "$STATE_DIR/$TREE".*.pass
+    say "FAIL the checks changed the working tree (${TREE:0:7} -> ${NEW_TREE:0:7}); commit or gitignore the generated files, then re-run" >&2
+    git status --short | head -n 20 >&2
+    exit 4
+fi
+say "all requested stages passed ($STAGES)"
+exit 0

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Tests bin/lib/prefire-verify (the pre-fire verification gate) and its wiring
+# into bin/post-plan-now, with stubbed PHPUnit / Infection / DB probe.
+#
+# Usage: bin/test-prefire-verify [case_name ...]
+# With no arguments every case runs; with arguments only the named cases run.
+# Prints `PASS <name>` / `FAIL <name>: <why>` per case. Exit 0 iff all pass.
+set -uo pipefail
+
+# shellcheck source=bin/lib/harness.sh
+. "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib/harness.sh"
+
+REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+GATE="$REPO/bin/lib/prefire-verify"
+PPN="$REPO/bin/post-plan-now"
+
+h_tmp TMP
+mkdir -p "$TMP/shims" "$TMP/runlog" "$TMP/Library/LaunchAgents"
+# Never touch real launchd, the keychain, or a shared /tmp log dir.
+printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n' > "$TMP/shims/security"
+printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$TMP/shims/launchctl"
+chmod +x "$TMP/shims/security" "$TMP/shims/launchctl"
+export PATH="$TMP/shims:$PATH"
+export IBL5_USAGE_GATE_STATE_DIR="$TMP/gate"
+mkdir -p "$IBL5_USAGE_GATE_STATE_DIR"
+export POSTPLAN_LOG_DIR="$TMP/runlog" PLAN_NOW_LOG_DIR="$TMP/runlog"
+unset CLAUDE_HEADLESS
+
+WHY=""      # failure reasons for the current case
+OUT=""      # combined stdout+stderr of the last run
+RC=0        # exit code of the last run
+
+note() { WHY="${WHY:+$WHY; }$*"; }
+want_rc() { [ "$RC" -eq "$1" ] || note "expected exit $1, got $RC"; }
+want_out() { grep -qF -- "$1" <<< "$OUT" || note "output lacks '$1'"; }
+refute_out() { if grep -qF -- "$1" <<< "$OUT"; then note "output unexpectedly has '$1'"; fi; }
+want_cnt() { # <counter> <n>
+    local got; got=$(cnt "$1")
+    [ "$got" -eq "$2" ] || note "counter $1 expected $2, got $got"
+}
+cnt() {
+    if [ -f "$CNT/$1" ]; then wc -l < "$CNT/$1" | tr -d ' '; else echo 0; fi
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Fixture: a fresh temp git repo plus stubs. Sets D (case dir), R (repo),
+# CNT (counter dir), PLAN (plan file path), and the PREFIRE_* seams.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+new_case() {
+    D=$(mktemp -d "$TMP/case.XXXXXX")
+    R="$D/repo"
+    CNT="$D/cnt"
+    PLAN="$D/plan.md"
+    mkdir -p "$R/ibl5/vendor/bin" "$CNT" "$D/stubs"
+    export CNT
+    unset STUB_PHPUNIT_RC STUB_MUT_MODE
+    cat > "$R/ibl5/vendor/bin/phpunit" <<'EOF'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo run >> "$CNT/phpunit"
+exit "${STUB_PHPUNIT_RC:-0}"
+EOF
+    cat > "$D/stubs/mutation" <<'EOF'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo run >> "$CNT/mutation"
+case "${STUB_MUT_MODE:-ok}" in
+    3672)
+        echo "2295 mutations were generated"
+        echo "491 mutants were escaped"
+        echo "[ERROR] The minimum required MSI percentage should be 100%, but actual is 78.6%"
+        exit 1 ;;
+    prereq) echo "Error: pcov is not loaded"; exit 3 ;;
+    *) echo "Mutation Score Indicator (MSI): 100%"; exit 0 ;;
+esac
+EOF
+    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho run >> "$CNT/probe"\nexit "${STUB_PROBE_RC:-0}"\n' > "$D/stubs/probe"
+    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho run >> "$CNT/excludes"\nexit 0\n' > "$D/stubs/excludes"
+    chmod +x "$R/ibl5/vendor/bin/phpunit" "$D/stubs/mutation" "$D/stubs/probe" "$D/stubs/excludes"
+    (
+        cd "$R" || exit 1
+        git init -q -b master
+        git config user.email t@example.com
+        git config user.name Test
+        printf 'a\n' > ibl5/tracked.txt
+        git add -A
+        git commit -q -m init
+    ) || { echo "HARNESS-SETUP: fixture repo failed" >&2; exit 2; }
+    export PREFIRE_PHPUNIT_CMD="vendor/bin/phpunit"
+    export PREFIRE_MUTATION_CMD="$D/stubs/mutation"
+    export PREFIRE_DB_PROBE_CMD="$D/stubs/probe"
+    export PREFIRE_EXCLUDES_CMD="$D/stubs/excludes"
+}
+
+# write_plan <row-line>...  — each argument is a full table row.
+write_plan() {
+    {
+        printf '# Plan\n\n## Verification Matrix\n\n'
+        printf '| # | What to verify | Test type | Timing | Test file / location |\n'
+        printf '|---|----------------|-----------|--------|----------------------|\n'
+        local r
+        for r in "$@"; do printf '%s\n' "$r"; done
+        printf '\nAll verification is automated.\n'
+    } > "$PLAN"
+}
+
+row() { # <n> <cmd>
+    printf '| %s | check %s | CLI-executable | post-impl | %s |' "$1" "$1" "$2"
+}
+
+# Three green rows that count their runs.
+green_plan() {
+    write_plan "$(row 1 "echo x >> $CNT/row1")" \
+               "$(row 2 "echo x >> $CNT/row2")" \
+               "$(row 3 "echo x >> $CNT/row3")"
+}
+
+run_gate() { # args passed to the gate; cwd = fixture repo
+    OUT=$(cd "$R" && "$GATE" --base master "$@" 2>&1); RC=$?
+}
+
+# The gate's per-worktree pass-record dir (git-path may be relative to the repo).
+state_dir() {
+    local p; p=$(cd "$R" && git rev-parse --git-path prefire-verify)
+    case "$p" in /*) printf '%s' "$p" ;; *) printf '%s/%s' "$R" "$p" ;; esac
+}
+pass_files() { # <glob>
+    local d f; d=$(state_dir)
+    [ -d "$d" ] || return 0
+    for f in "$d"/*; do
+        [ -e "$f" ] || continue
+        f=${f##*/}
+        if [[ "$f" =~ $1 ]]; then printf '%s\n' "$f"; fi
+    done
+}
+tree_hash() {
+    local idx rc
+    idx=$(mktemp "$TMP/idx.XXXXXX")
+    (cd "$R" && cp "$(git rev-parse --git-path index)" "$idx" \
+        && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" git add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 \
+        && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx" git write-tree)
+    rc=$?
+    rm -f "$idx"
+    return $rc
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Gate cases (matrix rows 7-21)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+test_matrix_row_failure_refuses_and_names_row() {
+    new_case
+    write_plan "$(row 1 true)" "$(row 2 true)" "$(row 3 'exit 7')"
+    run_gate --plan "$PLAN"
+    want_rc 1
+    want_out "FAIL matrix row 3 exited 7"
+    [ -z "$(pass_files '\.matrix\..*\.pass$')" ] || note "a matrix pass record exists"
+}
+
+test_unrun_row_refuses_without_gate_record() {
+    new_case
+    write_plan "$(row 1 "echo x >> $CNT/row1; exit 7")"
+    local d sha tree
+    d=$(state_dir); mkdir -p "$d"
+    sha=$(git hash-object "$PLAN")
+    tree=$(tree_hash)
+    printf 'All rows passed.\n' > "$D/ledger.md"
+    printf 'stage=matrix tree=OTHERTREE key=%s at=x by=prefire-verify\n' "$sha" \
+        > "$d/OTHERTREE.matrix.$sha.pass"
+    # Correct filename, wrong tree= field inside.
+    printf 'stage=matrix tree=WRONGTREE key=%s at=x by=prefire-verify\n' "$sha" \
+        > "$d/$tree.matrix.$sha.pass"
+    run_gate --plan "$PLAN"
+    want_rc 1
+    want_cnt row1 1
+}
+
+test_matrix_extract_skips_near_miss_rows() {
+    new_case
+    {
+        printf '## Verification Matrix\n\n'
+        printf '| # | What to verify | Test type | Timing | Test file / location |\n'
+        printf '|---|---|---|---|---|\n'
+        printf '| 1 | manual; run CLI-executable thing | Truly-manual | post-impl | echo manual |\n'
+        printf '| 2 | pre | CLI-executable | pre-impl | echo pre |\n'
+        printf '| 3 | plan-time (one-time-check: plan-time corpus diff) | CLI-executable | post-impl | echo onetime |\n'
+        printf '| 4 | merge | CLI-executable | post-impl | post-merge: echo merged |\n'
+        printf '| 5 | run-only | CLI-executable (run-only) | post-impl | echo runonly |\n'
+        printf '| 6 | pipe | CLI-executable | post-impl | echo a \\| tr a b |\n'
+        printf '\n## Next\n\n| 7 | after | CLI-executable | post-impl | echo outside |\n'
+    } > "$PLAN"
+    local got want
+    got=$(bash -c ". '$REPO/bin/lib/plan-matrix-rows.sh'; plan_matrix_rows '$PLAN'" 2>&1)
+    want=$'5\techo runonly\n6\techo a | tr a b'
+    [ "$got" = "$want" ] || note "expected exactly rows 5 and 6, got: $(printf '%s' "$got" | tr '\t\n' ' >')"
+}
+

+    new_case
+    printf '# Plan\n\n## Phase 1\n\nNothing here.\n' > "$PLAN"

+    want_out "no evidence to check"
+}

+    want_out "DB unreachable; matrix row 2 needs it"

+    run_gate --plan "$PLAN"; want_rc 0

+    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho run >> "$CNT/phpunit"\necho gen > ../generated.txt\nexit 0\n' > "$D/stubs/phpunit-mut"
+    chmod +x "$D/stubs/phpunit-mut"
+    export PREFIRE_PHPUNIT_CMD="$D/stubs/phpunit-mut"
+    run_gate --plan "$PLAN"
+    want_rc 4
+    want_out "changed the working tree"
+    [ -z "$(pass_files '\.phpunit\.pass$')" ] || note "a phpunit pass record exists"

+    run_gate
+    want_rc 0
+    want_out "SKIP matrix: no plan"

+    green_plan
+    export STUB_MUT_MODE=3672
+    run_gate --plan "$PLAN"

+    want_out "FAIL infection: below CI threshold"
+    want_out "491 mutants were escaped"

+
+test_mutation_diff_flags_match_ci() {
+    new_case
+    local wf="$REPO/.github/workflows/mutation-pr.yml" md="$REPO/bin/mutation-diff"
+    local flags f n=0 re
+    re='^--(min-msi|min-covered-msi|ignore-msi|git-diff-lines|only-covering|map-source|skip-initial|configuration=infection)'
+    flags=$(awk '/vendor\/bin\/infection/ {on=1} on {print} on && !/\\[[:space:]]*$/ {exit}' "$wf" \
+        | tr -s ' \\' '\n\n' | command grep -E -- "$re" || true)
+    for f in $flags; do
+        n=$((n + 1))
+        grep -qF -- "$f" "$md" || note "CI flag $f missing from bin/mutation-diff"
+    done
+    [ "$n" -ge 5 ] || note "extracted only $n CI flags; parsing broke"
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# post-plan-now cases (matrix rows 22-29)
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Builds MAIN (with origin) and a worktree WT on branch feat-x holding an
+# untracked file, so post-plan-now passes its nothing-to-ship check.
+new_ppn_case() {
+    new_case
+    local origin="$D/origin.git"
+    MAIN="$D/IBL5"
+    WT="$D/IBL5-worktrees/feat-x"
+    mkdir -p "$D/home"
+    git init -q --bare -b master "$origin"
+    mkdir -p "$MAIN/bin/lib" "$MAIN/ibl5/vendor/bin"
+    (
+        cd "$MAIN" || exit 1
+        git init -q -b master
+        git config user.email t@example.com
+        git config user.name Test
+        git remote add origin "file://$origin"
+        cp "$REPO/bin/lib/git-helpers.sh" bin/lib/git-helpers.sh
+        cp "$R/ibl5/vendor/bin/phpunit" ibl5/vendor/bin/phpunit
+        printf 'a\n' > ibl5/tracked.txt
+        git add -A
+        git commit -q -m init
+        git push -q origin master
+        git fetch -q origin
+        git worktree add -q -b feat-x "$WT" master
+    ) || { echo "HARNESS-SETUP: ppn fixture failed" >&2; exit 2; }
+    git -C "$WT" config branch.feat-x.iblBase master
+    printf 'new\n' > "$WT/NewTest.php"
+    R="$WT"   # the gate state helpers now point at the worktree
+    PLAN="$D/plan.md"
+    rm -f "$D"/runlog.* 2>/dev/null || true
+    rm -f "$POSTPLAN_LOG_DIR"/post-plan-now-feat-x-*.log 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+run_ppn() { # extra post-plan-now args; PPN_GATE overrides the gate path
+    OUT=$(cd "$WT" && \
+        BRANCH_BASE_OFFLINE=1 HOME="$D/home" \
+        POST_PLAN_MAIN_ROOT="$MAIN" POST_PLAN_SELF_BIN="$MAIN/bin" \
+        PREFIRE_VERIFY_SCRIPT="${PPN_GATE:-$GATE}" \
+        "$PPN" "$@" 2>&1); RC=$?
+}
+fired() { ls "$POSTPLAN_LOG_DIR"/post-plan-now-feat-x-*.log >/dev/null 2>&1; }
+
+test_post_plan_now_refuses_exit_9_on_gate_failure() {
+    new_ppn_case
+    write_plan "$(row 1 'exit 7')"
+    run_ppn --plan "$PLAN"
+    want_rc 9
+    want_out "pre-fire verification refused"
+    ! fired || note "post-plan-now launched despite a red gate"
+}
+
+test_post_plan_now_fires_when_gate_green() {
+    new_ppn_case
+    green_plan
+    run_ppn --plan "$PLAN"

+    fired || note "no runner log; post-plan-now did not get past the gate"
+}

+        n=$(wc -l < "$log" | tr -d ' ')
+        [ "$n" -eq 1 ] || note "bypass log has $n lines, expected 1"
+        grep -qF -- "fixture bypass reason ok" "$log" || note "bypass log lacks the reason"
+    else
+        note "no bypass log at $log"
+    fi
+    want_cnt phpunit 0
+}

+assert_step_6_9() { # <prompt-impl path>
+    local f="$1" l69 l68 l7 body
+    l69=$(grep -nF -- '## Step 6.9: Pre-Fire Verification Gate' "$f" | head -n 1 | cut -d: -f1)
+    if [ -z "$l69" ]; then
+        note "no Step 6.9 heading"
+        return 0
+    fi
+    l68=$(grep -nF -- '## Step 6.8:' "$f" | head -n 1 | cut -d: -f1)
+    l7=$(grep -nF -- '## Step 7: Write Handoff File' "$f" | head -n 1 | cut -d: -f1)
+    [ -n "$l68" ] || note "no Step 6.8 heading"
+    [ -n "$l7" ] || note "no Step 7 heading"
+    [ -n "$l68" ] && [ "$l69" -gt "$l68" ] || note "Step 6.9 is not after Step 6.8"
+    [ -n "$l7" ] && [ "$l69" -lt "$l7" ] || note "Step 6.9 is not before Step 7"
+    if [ -n "$l7" ] && [ "$l69" -lt "$l7" ]; then
+        body=$(sed -n "${l69},$((l7 - 1))p" "$f")
+        local s
+        for s in "--stage matrix" "--stage phpunit" "--stage infection"; do
+            grep -qF -- "$s" <<< "$body" || note "Step 6.9 does not name '$s'"
+        done
+    fi
+}
+
+test_prompt_impl_step_6_9_precedes_step_7() {
+    assert_step_6_9 "$REPO/bin/automouse/prompt-impl"
+}
+
+test_prompt_impl_missing_step_6_9_heading_fails() {

+    grep -vF -- '## Step 6.9: Pre-Fire Verification Gate' \
+        "$REPO/bin/automouse/prompt-impl" > "$fixture"
+    assert_step_6_9 "$fixture"
+    if [ "$WHY" = "no Step 6.9 heading" ]; then
+        WHY=""
+    else
+        WHY="a missing heading must fail, got: '${WHY}'"
+    fi
+}

+test_db_probe_does_not_read_callers_stdin() {
+    new_case
+    write_plan "$(row 1 "echo x >> $CNT/row1; bin/db-query 'SELECT 1'")"
+    # The probe fails if it can read a line, so an inherited stdin refuses.
+    local saved="${PREFIRE_DB_PROBE_CMD:-}"
+    export PREFIRE_DB_PROBE_CMD='! read -r _line'
+    run_gate --plan "$PLAN" <<< "caller stdin"
+    refute_out "DB unreachable"

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Runner
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+ALL_CASES="
+test_matrix_row_failure_refuses_and_names_row
+test_unrun_row_refuses_without_gate_record
+test_matrix_extract_skips_near_miss_rows
+test_plan_without_matrix_refuses
+test_phpunit_red_refuses
+test_db_down_fails_closed_naming_row
+test_all_green_passes_and_records
+test_cache_hit_skips_rerun

+test_checks_mutating_tree_refuse
+test_adhoc_no_plan_runs_phpunit_and_infection
+test_infection_below_threshold_refuses_3672

+test_infection_prereq_missing_fails_closed
+test_mutation_diff_flags_match_ci
+test_post_plan_now_refuses_exit_9_on_gate_failure

+test_post_plan_now_adhoc_no_plan_skips_matrix_only
+test_bypass_logs_line_and_fires
+test_bypass_refused_under_headless
+test_bypass_short_reason_rejected
+test_rebase_only_skips_gate
+test_missing_gate_script_refuses
+test_prompt_impl_step_6_9_precedes_step_7
+test_prompt_impl_missing_step_6_9_heading_fails
+test_stdin_reading_row_does_not_swallow_later_rows
+test_db_probe_does_not_read_callers_stdin
+"
+
+if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then CASES="$*"; else CASES="$ALL_CASES"; fi
+
+for name in $CASES; do
+    if ! declare -F "$name" >/dev/null; then
+        echo "FAIL $name: no such case"
+        H_FAIL=$((H_FAIL + 1))
+        continue
+    fi
+    WHY=""
+    "$name"
+    if [ -z "$WHY" ]; then
+        echo "PASS $name"
+        H_PASS=$((H_PASS + 1))
+    else
+        echo "FAIL $name: $WHY"
+        printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | sed -n '1,15p' | sed 's/^/    | /'
+        H_FAIL=$((H_FAIL + 1))
+    fi
+done
+
+h_done

+# ADR-0227: Pre-fire verification gate in post-plan-now
+
+**Status:** Accepted
+**Date:** 2026-11-03
+**Deciders:** ajaynicolas
+
+## Context
+
+PR #3672 shipped with 491 of 2295 mutants escaped and CI's per-PR Infection job red. Its implementation ran no Infection before firing. Two paths fire a ship: a human or interactive session calling `bin/post-plan-now`, and the automouse runner calling `post-plan-now --foreground` from the handoff file. Neither checked that verification had run.
+
+## Decision
+
+- One gate script, `bin/lib/prefire-verify`, is called from `bin/post-plan-now` before any launch. It exits 9 on refusal.
+- Automouse's `bin/automouse/prompt-impl` Step 6.9 runs the same script stage by stage, so the impl agent can fix failures while it still has the tree.
+- The gate re-runs every check and trusts no implementer-written ledger. Pass records are keyed by tree hash and written only by the gate.
+- Infection runs through `bin/mutation-diff`, so CI's flags and MSI 100 live in one place (the per-PR check of ADR-0145).
+- The gate fails closed: a missing prerequisite, a timed-out stage, or a missing record all mean no fire.
+- The bypass, `--skip-verify=<reason>`, is human-only, needs a reason of at least 15 characters, is refused under `CLAUDE_HEADLESS`, and is logged to `prefire-verify-bypass.log` in the main checkout's `.git`.
+
+## Extend-before-add
+
+No existing host owns this. `bin/lib/plan-matrix-assertions` checks that a diff footprint exists and never executes a row. `bin/post-plan-now` is the host, but the same logic must also be callable stage by stage from the impl prompt, so it lives in `bin/lib/` and is called from both places. The matrix parser moved from `bin/check-plan` into the shared `bin/lib/plan-matrix-rows.sh`, so there is one parser.
+
+## Alternatives Considered
+
+- **Trust a ledger the implementer writes.** Rejected because: the check would then rest on the claim it exists to verify.
+- **Gate only in CI.** Rejected because: CI already has the Infection job and `#3672` shipped red anyway; the failure must reach the implementer before the fire.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- Negative: the first fire on a new tree costs a full PHPUnit run plus a changed-file mutation run.
+- Positive: a stage the impl session could not finish within its 600 s cap reruns at the fire point, inside the runner's remaining budget.
+- Neutral: ad-hoc runs with no plan keep PHPUnit and Infection and skip the matrix stage.
+- Neutral: fleet rescues (`--pr`) are gated too, and `--rebase-only` is exempt because it pushes no new content.
+
+## References
+
+- `bin/lib/prefire-verify`: the gate and its pass records.
+- `bin/test-prefire-verify`: the harness.
+- `bin/post-plan-now`: the fire point and exit 9.
+- `bin/automouse/prompt-impl`: Step 6.9.
+- `bin/mutation-diff`: the shared Infection runner.
+- `bin/lib/plan-matrix-rows.sh`: the shared matrix parser.
+- `.github/workflows/mutation-pr.yml`: the CI side of the same check.
+- `ibl5/docs/decisions/0145-mutation-pr-required-own-workflow.md`: the per-PR mutation check.

+# Sized for one 600 s foreground Bash call (prompt-impl Step 6.9): a row starts only
+# inside the 300 s budget and can then take at most 120 s baseline + 120 s mutated.
+XM_TIMEOUT=30
+XM_MAX_TIMEOUT=120
+XM_BUDGET=300
+XM_CHILD=""
+
+xm_cleanup() { # stop a running lib child, then restore any journalled mutation
+    if [ -n "$XM_CHILD" ]; then
+        kill -TERM "$XM_CHILD" 2>/dev/null
+        wait "$XM_CHILD" 2>/dev/null
+        XM_CHILD=""
+    fi
+    "$XM_LIB" recover --root "$ROOT" >/dev/null 2>&1
+}
+
+stage_exec_mutations() {
+    local xm_key recs log rc
+    if [ -z "$PLAN" ]; then
+        say "SKIP exec-mutations: no plan (ad-hoc path)"
+        return 0
+    fi
+    xm_key=$(git hash-object "$PLAN")
+    cache_hit exec-mutations "$xm_key" && return 0
+
+    recs=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/prefire-xm.XXXXXX") || return 3
+    "$XM_LIB" parse --root "$ROOT" "$PLAN" > "$recs" 2>&1; rc=$?
+    if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then
+        say "FAIL exec-mutations: PARSE-FAILED: $(head -1 "$recs"); fix the plan's mutation block" >&2
+        rm -f "$recs"; return 1
+    elif [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
+        say "FAIL exec-mutations: plan-exec-mutations parse exited $rc" >&2
+        rm -f "$recs"; return 3
+    fi
+    if [ ! -s "$recs" ]; then
+        rm -f "$recs"
+        say "SKIP exec-mutations: the plan has no Executable Mutations rows"
+        return 0
+    fi
+    rm -f "$recs"
+    if ! command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        say "FAIL exec-mutations prerequisite missing: gtimeout or timeout (brew install coreutils)" >&2
+        return 3
+    fi

+    log="$STATE_DIR/$TREE.exec-mutations.log"
+    # The lib traps its own signals and reverts. This stage adds two things: it runs the
+    # lib in the background so a signal interrupts `wait` at once (bash defers traps
+    # while a foreground child runs), and it forwards the signal and runs recover itself.
+    trap 'xm_cleanup' EXIT
+    trap 'xm_cleanup; exit 130' INT
+    trap 'xm_cleanup; exit 143' TERM
+    trap 'xm_cleanup; exit 129' HUP
